85b8949befe852a7: GEORGE TOWN: Hong Kong actor Edison Chen is making his return to the big screen after a 10-year hiatus, starring in a Chinese New Year film currently being shot in Malaysia.
The 45-year-old actor attended the film's lensing ceremony here on Sept 17, alongside veteran actor Anthony Wong and Samuel Pang.
Cheers erupted when Chen was handed the microphone, reflecting his enduring popularity among fans.
Chen had previously scaled back his acting commitments to focus on his fashion business and spend more time with his family.
Speaking at the ceremony, he said he was excited to return to filmmaking.
"It's really been a long time, so I'm very excited to start filming. I'll do my best and continue to work hard. Thank you, everyone," he said in a news report yesterday.
Wong, 65, also expressed his happiness at returning to Penang, where he had not filmed for a decade.
However, he joked that the city's famous food had already taken a toll on his waistline.
"Penang is not only beautiful. The food is also irresistible. I've eaten so much that I've gained weight. I'll have to lose weight next," Wong said.
For Pang, 49, the production marks his first visit to the island. He said he had already developed a fondness for the local food and was grateful for the opportunity to work with Chen and Wong again.
"I'm very grateful to the director for giving me the opportunity to work with Anthony and Edison again," Pang said.
The film, which began shooting on Sept 7, is scheduled to wrap by the end of the month, with filming also taking place in Kuala Lumpur, China and Italy.

cf5f1cd61d32d088: SEMPORNA: The inaugural Igal-Igal Festival at Mantabuan Island here has been proposed as an annual community-based event that could be expanded to other islands within Tun Sakaran Marine Park (TSMP).

State Tourism, Culture and Environment Ministry deputy permanent secretary Rimi Repin said the initiative could provide island communities with a platform to showcase their cultural heritage, traditions and tourism products.
She said Igal-Igal represented more than a traditional dance, describing it as part of the Bajau community's heritage, identity and pride.
"Igal-Igal is among the cultural treasures that hold their own unique value and have been passed down from generation to generation.
"The beauty of its dance movements, accompanied by traditional music and its distinctive performances, reflects the richness of the culture and creativity of the local community.
"We want Igal-Igal to be recognised not only among the local community, but also introduced to visitors from Malaysia and abroad as part of Semporna's cultural identity.

"I welcome this aspiration because community-based programmes have the potential to become an ongoing platform for promoting cultural heritage and the unique tourism attractions of the marine park areas," she said when officiating the two-day 2026 Igal-Igal Festival at Mantabuan Island here today.

The inaugural festival was organised by the Mantabuan Island community and Koperasi Alam Laut Silangau Semporna Berhad (KOPSI), with Brand Borneo Tours, Travel and Experiences Sdn Bhd as co-organiser, in collaboration with the Tun Sakaran Marine Park management and relevant agencies.
Mantabuan is one of eight islands under Tun Sakaran Marine Park. The others are Bohey Dulang, Bodgaya, Tetagan, Selakan, Sebangkat, Maiga and Sibuan.

Rimi said activities featured in the festival, including environmental awareness programmes, arts and cultural exhibitions, traditional music, traditional food and community activities, could help raise awareness about protecting the islands and marine ecosystems.

She said expanding the festival to other islands, with the cooperation of all stakeholders, could create opportunities for more island communities to participate in tourism-related economic activities.
These could include handicraft production, traditional food preparation, tourism services and other supporting activities.
However, Rimi said the success of an annual festival should not be measured solely by visitor numbers or the vibrancy of the event.
"It should also be measured by the benefits returned to the community and its impact on the preservation of cultural heritage and the environment," she said.
Rimi also stressed the importance of ensuring that tourism development in Tun Sakaran Marine Park was carried out responsibly and sustainably.
"We cannot separate tourism development from our responsibility to protect the environment," she said.
Also present were marine park manager Ghazali Pe Hindi and co-organisers Jasni Kanti and Anton Ngui.

9a9f8eae62f37ef9: SEPTEMBER 19 — I understand why the Government is seeking a practical and durable solution to the presence of large numbers of Myanmar nationals in Malaysia, including the Rohingya. Malaysia cannot be expected to carry this burden indefinitely, and diplomacy requires engagement with difficult actors and the pursuit of solutions that serve both humanitarian and national interests.
But diplomacy is not simply about opening doors to anyone. It is about knowing what we want to achieve, building leverage and securing commitments before we make concessions.
That is why I do not believe that inviting Min Aung Hlaing to Malaysia is the right diplomatic move at this stage.
This is not about refusing to communicate with Myanmar or its leaders. It is about how we conduct diplomacy and what political value we choose to confer through that engagement.

A Prime Ministerial invitation gives Myanmar’s military leadership political access, international visibility and legitimacy. That is precisely why such an invitation should follow meaningful political movement, rather than precede it.

In serious negotiations, we establish our objectives, build leverage, seek reciprocal commitments and test whether the other side is prepared to change. We should not offer the diplomatic prize before the negotiation has even begun.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
The author believes that inviting Min Aung Hlaing to Malaysia is not the right diplomatic move at this stage. — AFP pic
What has Myanmar actually committed to?

Today, the military continues to use violence against civilians, while political repression and violence continue across the country. There has been no indication that Naypyidaw is considering any amendment or abolition of the 1982 Citizenship Law which stripped

the Rohingya of their citizenship. They refuse even to refer to the Rohingya by their ethnic name — choosing instead to call them by the exclusionary and derogatory term “Bengali”. The situation facing the Rohingya in Rakhine State remains deeply insecure and legal protections are non-existent.

Of particular concern is the forced conscription and recruitment of Rohingya by the Myanmar military to fight the Arakan Army. This move is profoundly dangerous and destabilising. Forcing the already displaced and oppressed Rohingya into an ethnic conflict risks further turning them into targets, fuelling new cycles of violence and hatred, and triggering new waves of displacement.
More fundamentally, it risks cementing their permanent exclusion from Myanmar — making the conditions for safe, dignified and sustainable repatriation impossible to establish.
Repatriation cannot be separated from political reality

You cannot create the conditions for repatriation by forcing the very people you claim you want to bring home to fight in the conflict. That is a recipe for deeper hostility, further displacement and permanent exclusion.

There is also a fundamental political reality that Malaysia must recognise: the Myanmar military does not control most of Rakhine State. After five years of post-coup conflict, the Arakan Army has de facto control of the vast majority of the State.

Whatever one’s view of the Arakan Army, any serious discussion about the future of the Rohingya and the conditions for their return must take account of who exercises authority on the ground. That means that a bilateral discussion with Naypyidaw alone — and in particular with Min Aung Hlaing — cannot determine the conditions under which Rohingya will live and return in areas controlled by another armed authority.
This is why Malaysia should use its diplomatic weight differently.
Malaysia knows how to navigate conflict and difficult negotiations
Malaysia is not new to difficult political negotiations or conflict mediation.

Our experience in Mindanao and Southern Thailand has demonstrated the importance of understanding the interests and positions of different parties, building confidence, maintaining channels with difficult actors and ensuring that commitments can be monitored and implemented. These experiences have also taught us that dealing with conflict requires more than access to one powerful actor or a single high-level meeting.

Malaysia knows the difference between engagement and effective political negotiation. We know that access is not the same as leverage, that a meeting is not a negotiation, and that a promise is not a political settlement.
We should bring that experience to Myanmar.
A sustainable political settlement cannot be negotiated by one party alone, particularly when that party does not control most of the territory in which the Rohingya are expected to return.
Malaysia must protect the credibility it has built
There is another reason why we must approach this carefully: Malaysia’s international credibility and our commitment to international law.

In January 2020, the International Court of Justice unanimously imposed legally binding provisional measures requiring Myanmar to protect the Rohingya from acts prohibited by the Genocide Convention and, specifically, to ensure that its military does not commit such acts.

On 27 November 2024, the Prosecutor of the International Criminal Court applied for an arrest warrant for Min Aung Hlaing, alleging his criminal responsibility for the crimes against humanity of deportation and persecution of the Rohingya committed during the 2017 violence; that application remains for the Court’s judges to determine. These are not peripheral considerations.

Malaysia has rightly spoken forcefully on Gaza, insisting on international law, protection of civilians and accountability. We have argued that the lives and rights of civilians cannot become secondary to political convenience.
The same principles must apply to the Rohingya.

This is not about equating Gaza and Myanmar. They are different conflicts. It is about demonstrating that Malaysia’s commitment to international law and civilian protection is consistent and universal.
That consistency matters to our standing in Asean, in the Muslim world and in the wider international community.

Malaysia has built its foreign policy reputation over many years on being balanced, independent and principled — engaging even when we disagree, maintaining channels of communication while standing by our principles, and seeking practical solutions without abandoning international law.
This balance has been one of our diplomatic strengths. We should be building on it, not undermining it.

If Malaysia now appears to confer political legitimacy and prominence on the very military leadership facing international accountability for atrocities against the Rohingya, the reputational cost will not be confined to this particular issue. It risks raising wider questions about the consistency and credibility of Malaysia’s foreign policy.

Malaysia’s influence has never depended on being the biggest country or the most powerful country. It has depended in considerable measure on the credibility of our diplomacy — our ability to speak to different sides, maintain trust and act with principle while remaining pragmatic.
That is an asset we should protect, not spend lightly.

Malaysia can pursue diplomacy without legitimising Min Aung Hlaing. There are channels for communication that do not require us to confer the political legitimacy and prominence that a Prime Ministerial invitation would provide.
Malaysia’s engagement must be broader
Malaysia should start with Myanmar’s regional neighbours and engage the wider range of Myanmar stakeholders.

Bangladesh carries the immediate burden of the Rohingya refugee crisis. Thailand shares a long border with Myanmar and has dealt directly for decades with conflict, displacement and refugee movements.

Malaysia has already demonstrated during our 2025 Asean Chairmanship that we can engage a broad range of Myanmar stakeholders, including the military, democratic and ethnic political actors, and both Rakhine and Rohingya representatives, while maintaining our diplomatic position. We should build on that experience, not narrow our diplomacy to the Myanmar military alone.

Malaysia should use the relationships developed during our Chairmanship to engage Myanmar’s democratic and ethnic political stakeholders, Rohingya representatives and those exercising authority on the ground, alongside Bangladesh and Thailand and our wider international partners.
This is not about recognising or legitimising any particular actor. It is about engaging the political realities that will determine whether any agreement can actually be implemented.
From there, Malaysia can build a wider diplomatic coalition, including Türkiye, China and the United Nations.
One essential element should be the independent third-party monitoring of any future Rohingya return, including an appropriate role for the United Nations.

If Myanmar is genuinely serious about safe and sustainable return, it should be prepared to accept independent verification. Such monitoring would help establish whether return is genuinely voluntary and whether people remain safe after they return. It would also prevent the process from being controlled or manipulated by any one party.
The objective should not simply be to negotiate the movement of people across a border. It should be to create the political and security conditions in which people can actually return and remain.
What Malaysia can offer

Our leverage lies precisely in what we are able to offer — and when we choose to offer it. That leverage should be used to secure meaningful commitments, not surrendered at the outset of the negotiation.

Malaysia has something valuable to bring to this crisis: our diplomatic credibility, our relationships across the region and our experience in navigating difficult political processes. We have dealt with governments, armed groups, political movements and communities in conflict. We should draw on that experience now.
The invitation should be the consequence of meaningful political movement, not the inducement offered in advance.
Malaysia can be pragmatic without abandoning principle. Indeed, our principles are part of our diplomatic strength.
Malaysia should use that strength wisely — protecting our diplomatic credibility, preserving our leverage and positioning ourselves to lead a serious regional effort on Myanmar.
* Tan Sri Datuk Seri Dr Syed Hamid Albar is the former minister of foreign affairs of Malaysia and chair of the Malaysian Advisory Group on Myanmar

0a0acb6ed1d02816: NAGOYA: The 20th Asian Games opened in Japan on Saturday with a message of unity following a troubled build-up to the multi-sport spectacular that has more athletes than the Olympics.
There were however a large number of empty seats at the 30,000-capacity stadium in Nagoya, where a subdued crowd saw a colourful opening ceremony with the main stage in the shape of a giant heart.
Japan's Emperor and Empress were given a respectful reception as they took their seats, with International Olympic Committee president Kirsty Coventry also in attendance.

The first gold medal will be won on Sunday morning, likely in the men's individual triathlon, as the continent's finest athletes compete in more than 40 sports before the curtain comes down on October 4.
The event in Nagoya and Aichi prefecture has 2028 Olympics places up for grabs in seven sports and will be graced by global stars and fast-rising prodigies.
But it has been dogged by a series of problems in the lead-up.
The more than 11,000 athletes and 6,000 officials stretched organisers to the limit as they scrambled to find accommodation for everyone.
To save money there is no traditional athletes' village, competitors instead staying in a combination of temporary container-style huts, hotels and cruise ship the Costa Serena.
There was a record deluge last week which flooded parts of Nagoya and now a typhoon is approaching eastern Japan threatening further disruption in the coming days.
Some athletes were left stranded at the airport when transport failed to turn up and several teams have complained about the quality of the huts, including the beds being too short.
In the latest mishap, North Korea's national anthem was played on Friday for South Korea's men's hockey team.
- Cheers, empty seats -
Two-time Asian Games silver medallist Zahra Kiani was a flag-bearer for Iran and hopes to win another medal in the Chinese martial art of wushu – by watching how it's done on YouTube.
"I have been training with movies. I watch videos of Chinese athletes and I try to copy them," she said.
The Olympic Council of Asia said the continent's premier sporting event, featuring 45 countries and territories, came at a vital moment.

"The opening ceremony message is to show and demonstrate the unity of Asia against the conflicts around Asia (and) the political conflicts of the Middle East," OCA president Sheikh Joaan bin Hamad Al-Thani said before the show swung into action.
There was no mistaking, however, the rows of empty seats, despite organisers saying all tickets had been taken.
Apart from Japan's athletes, the biggest cheer was reserved for China's competitors as they filed into the arena.
China will again expect to top the medals table after winning a whopping 201 golds and 383 medals on home soil in Hangzhou at the Covid-delayed Games in 2023.
- Prodigies in spotlight -
Basketball, football and cricket are among the sports already under way.
As always at the Asian Games – which started in 1951 – Olympic staples such as athletics and swimming will sit side-by-side with regional favourites like sepak takraw and kabaddi.
There will be eSports, breakdancing and BMX cycling. Padel and MMA will make their Asian Games debuts.
Among those competing will be Philippine tennis sensation Alexandra Eala and a pair of prodigies in 15-year-old Indian cricketer Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and 13-year-old Chinese swimmer Yu Zidi.
Taiwan boxer Lin Yu-ting will also be competing, two years after she won Paris Olympics gold in the middle of a major gender row that saw her eligibility questioned.
North Korea will have more than 100 athletes competing across 14 sports, aiming to "bring joy to Marshal Kim Jong Un."
Sooryavanshi will be part of an India cricket team looking to make a statement before the sport returns to the Olympics in Los Angeles after an absence of 128 years.
India could face bitter rivals Pakistan in the final at Nagoya's new purpose-built cricket ground – if rain does not intervene.-AFP

5e3df7581da9459a: KUALA LUMPUR: Transport Minister Anthony Loke will resign from the cabinet following the Pardons Board's decision to grant former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak conditional house arrest.
Loke, who is also DAP secretary-general, said the party's other ministers and deputy ministers would remain in the government.

"After discussions and taking into account the reactions from the CEC (Central Executive Committee), I will resign as transport minister, while the rest will remain in the government," he told reporters at DAP headquarters in Jalan Pudu today.
Loke announced his decision after a three-hour CEC meeting to discuss the party's stance on Najib's conditional house arrest.
He said he would formally tender his resignation letter to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in due course.
Loke said his decision to step down was a personal stance, while the other ministers would remain in their positions to maintain political stability.
"If all DAP ministers were to resign, the government could collapse, leading to political instability, which is precisely what our opponents are waiting for.
"DAP would not allow opposition forces to exploit the situation," he said.

Loke said DAP respected the royal prerogative exercised by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, but that the decision remained difficult for the party and the public to accept given the scale of the 1MDB scandal.
"The 1MDB scandal is a major corruption crisis that has plagued the nation for a decade.
"DAP has always fought for truth and justice, and those responsible must face the full weight of the law," he said.
He also assured the public that operations at the Transport Ministry and ongoing national infrastructure projects would continue without disruption during the transition.

Yesterday, the Federal Territories Pardons Board announced that Najib, 73, had been granted a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of a RM50 million fine.
The decision was made at the 64th meeting of the Pardons Board for the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur, Labuan and Putrajaya at Istana Negara.
​The Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister's Department said His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, had consented to the conditional pardon.

4a9bd17ba8df2781: KUANTAN: A mother has claimed that her 14-year-old son and another Form Two student were assaulted by five students at a religious school hostel in Bukit Ibam, Rompin, resulting in injuries to various parts of their bodies.

Siti Rohani Yusof, 40, said the first incident occurred at about midnight on Sept 12 when the two students were called into a hostel room, had their heads covered, and were allegedly beaten, with her son assaulted for about two hours, and his friend for about two-and-a-half hours.
"My son did not dare tell anyone after the incident for fear of being beaten again. Only on Tuesday did he inform the warden and teachers about what happened," she said here today.
Rohani alleged that her son was assaulted again on Sept 15 by the same students using a broomstick, with one holding the stick while another kicked him.
She said her son contacted his father, who informed the warden, before she went to the school the following day.
She said the senior students allegedly kicked, pinched, slapped and punched her son, besides hitting him with a broomstick.
Her son was taken to Muadzam Shah Hospital for a medical examination, including X-rays, after a police report was lodged at the Muadzam Shah police station.
She also said she had decided to transfer her son to another school because of concerns over his safety.
Rompin police chief Sharif Shai Sharif Mondoi confirmed that a report had been received regarding a fight involving two Form Two students at a hostel of a religious school in Bukit Ibam.
He said a preliminary investigation found that both victims were called to a hostel room by five male students, comprising three Form Five students and two Form Four students.

"The cause of the incident was that the first victim skipped religious lectures, while the second victim was complicit with the first. Both victims were beaten by all the suspects," he said in a statement today.
He said five suspects had been detained before being released on police bail, with the case being investigated under Section 147 of the Penal Code for use of force or violence.
997d23164ce73910: BATU KAWAN: The government aims to finalise the drafting of a new e-commerce Bill this year, said Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali.
He said the ministry had approved a policy decision to repeal the Electronic Commerce Act 2006 and replace it with a new, more comprehensive law.
However, he said the process would require coordination between ministries and extensive engagement with stakeholders, including e-commerce platforms, service providers and industry players.

"We know that e-commerce is a broad and comprehensive area, so it requires extensive engagement with stakeholders. We need to examine the matter thoroughly, and I hope it can be finalised," he told reporters after launching the 2026 Consumer Festival (CONFEST 2026) at Batu Kawan Stadium here today.

Armizan said two committees had also been established to expedite the drafting of the Bill, including to facilitate coordination between the ministry, the Communications Ministry and the Digital Ministry.
He said matters currently being fine-tuned included the division of responsibilities among the ministries and relevant agencies, as well as regulatory mechanisms for e-commerce platforms.
The next stage would require a regulatory impact assessment (RIA) in collaboration with the Malaysia Productivity Corporation (MPC) before the Bill is submitted for further consideration.

Among the proposals being studied is the introduction of a licensing regime for e-commerce platforms, particularly in view of the influx of goods from overseas, consumer safety and the sustainability of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
However, Armizan said regulation must be balanced to avoid hampering the growth of the e-commerce sector, which provides convenience to consumers and serves as a source of income for traders.
"We want more comprehensive and conducive regulation, but at the same time, we do not want to hamper the growth of e-commerce," he said.

The government had previously expressed its intention to expedite the drafting of the e-commerce Bill to strengthen the regulation and accountability of platforms, sellers and consumers, given that the Electronic Commerce Act 2006 does not provide a comprehensive legal framework to regulate various aspects of e-commerce.
8fcb09f954ff5fbe: JAKARTA: Malaysia mendapat lampu hijau dari Indonesia untuk menghantar bantuan bagi membantu memadamkan kebakaran hutan dan tanah yang menyebabkan jerebu rentas sempadan seterusnya menjejaskan ruang udara negara jiran termasuk Malaysia.
Timbalan Perdana Menteri, Zahid Hamidi, berkata persetujuan itu diberikan ketika pertemuannya dengan Presiden Indonesia Prabowo Subianto di Istana Hambalang sempena dengan lawatan kerja ke Jakarta.

“Presiden Prabowo telah menyambut dengan baik, ertinya memberikan keizinan terhadap tawaran Malaysia untuk sama-sama menangani permasalahan jerebu dan kebakaran di Kalimantan,” katanya dalam sidang media hari ini.

Bantuan ditawarkan Malaysia merangkumi sebuah pesawat Bombardier CL-415MP, tiga helikopter serta 52 pegawai dan anggota daripada Agensi Pengurusan Bencana Negara (Nadma), Agensi Penguatkuasaan Maritim Malaysia (APMM) dan Tentera Udara Diraja Malaysia (TUDM).

Zahid, yang juga pengerusi Jawatankuasa Pengurusan Bencana Pusat, berkata Menteri Luar Mohamad Hasan diminta menyelaraskan bantuan itu dengan Nadma, APMM, Jabatan Meteorologi Malaysia, TUDM, Jabatan Bomba dan Penyelamat Malaysia (JBPM) serta pihak berkaitan.

“Oleh kerana keizinan telah diperoleh daripada Presiden Prabowo, tentu koordinasi pada peringkat kementerian, jabatan dan agensi harus dilakukan. Saya mengharapkan agar Kementerian Luar, dalam melakukan koordinasi ini, dapat memastikan semua pihak yang akan terlibat dalam operasi ini melakukan usaha yang terselaras,” katanya.

Beliau berkata, bantuan itu bukan hanya untuk jangka pendek bagi memadamkan kebakaran, sebaliknya kedua-dua negara turut berbincang dan mencapai persetujuan untuk merancang langkah jangka panjang bagi memastikan masalah jerebu akibat kebakaran tidak berulang.

Zahid berkata, dalam pertemuan itu Prabowo turut memaklumkan sehingga kini masih terdapat 1,426 titik panas di Kalimantan, manakala tindakan perundangan telah diambil pemerintah Indonesia terhadap 95 syarikat yang terlibat dalam kebakaran secara terbuka di kawasan di kepulauan Borneo itu.

Ditanya sama ada terdapat syarikat Malaysia dalam kalangan 95 syarikat berkenaan, Ahmad Zahid berkata tiada maklumat mengenainya diberikan setakat ini, dan pihak Indonesia sedang meneliti jika terdapat penglibatan dari Malaysia.

“Syarikat-syarikat itu didaftarkan atas nama syarikat di Indonesia. Mungkin dari segi pemegang saham, terdapat beberapa jumlah kecil syarikat-syarikat berkenaan dimiliki oleh pemegang saham dari Malaysia,” katanya.

Beliau berkata Malaysia menyambut baik langkah yang telah diambil Indonesia dan sebagai negara jiran terdekat akan terus memberikan kerjasama dalam usaha menangani isu kebakaran serta jerebu rentas sempadan, khususnya kesannya terhadap Sarawak.
53c31bfb5f48860c: JAKARTA: Ties between parties in the unity government remain good following the Pardons Board's decision to grant Datuk Seri Najib Razak conditional house arrest, says Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
Zahid said the decision by the Pardons Board, chaired by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, was constitutional.

"Certainly, His Majesty has taken various aspects into consideration, and if any party wants to question the King's decision, then it would not be in line with the provisions of the Federal Constitution," he told a press conference.
He said Umno and Barisan Nasional maintained that the law must always be adhered to, adding that this was clear from his previous statements.
"Our relationship (with other parties in the unity government) is still good.
"We may be politicians, but when it comes to administrative matters, we are professional and there are no problems because decisions made by the Cabinet are a collective responsibility."
He said ties between Cabinet members were also good on a personal level.
His comments come amid mixed reactions to the conditional house arrest granted to former prime minister Najib.
Umno yesterday welcomed the Pardons Board's decision and began fundraising for the RM50 million fine Najib must pay to be allowed to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.

Last night, the Pakatan Harapan Presidential Council said no one was above the law and that anyone convicted of an offence must serve their sentence in accordance with the Federal Constitution and the law.
The council said it stood firmly behind Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's position, as well as the advice given by the Attorney-General and Federal Territories Minister to the Pardons Board.

Earlier today, Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said it was inappropriate for anyone to portray the exercise of the constitutional power of pardon as an act of being "above the law".
a94272c5d16dc28d: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 19 — A total of 17 areas nationwide recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at unhealthy levels as of 4 pm today.

According to data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), Sarawak recorded seven areas with unhealthy readings, namely IPD Serian (178), Kuching (171), Sri Aman (168), Samarahan (164), Sibu (157), Sarikei (152) and Bintulu (106).
In Johor, three areas recorded unhealthy readings, namely Larkin (158), Pasir Gudang (155) and Tangkak (102), followed by Kuala Lumpur with Cheras (149) and Batu Muda (121).
Seri Manjung in Perak recorded a reading of 159, while Shah Alam in Selangor recorded 152.
Putrajaya (121), Nilai in Negeri Sembilan (111) and Bukit Rambai in Melaka (108) were also at unhealthy levels.
Meanwhile, 38 other areas recorded moderate readings, while 12 areas recorded good air quality.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and 301 and above hazardous. — Bernama
023f97e46aaccb43: KUALA LUMPUR: Fly FM has stopped playing Ed Sheeran's songs following the controversy surrounding US rapper Macklemore's removal from the singer's Loop Tour.

In an Instagram post yesterday, the English-language station announced that Sheeran's music had been removed from its playlist, alongside a photograph of the British singer and the words: "Off our playlist! Some things matter more than music."
In the accompanying caption, Fly FM said it supported Palestinians and artists who used their platforms to voice their views on the issue.
The station also said music should provide a space for people to speak up rather than silence issues.
"You may have seen the news about Macklemore being dropped from the Loop Tour after he spoke up for Palestine.
"We want to make our position clear. Fly FM stands with Palestine. We also stand with artists who use their voices for what they believe in.
"Music should give people space to speak, not silence them. We stand with Palestine. We stand with artists who speak up for them," it said.
The move drew support from some users in the comments section, with some calling for more artists perceived to support Israel to be removed from the station's playlist.

In Ireland, Classic Hits Radio has also removed Sheeran's music from its playlist "for the foreseeable future" following feedback from listeners over the controversy surrounding Macklemore's departure from the US leg of the tour.
The station's decision followed the withdrawal of several support acts, including Irish singer-songwriter Aaron Rowe and Irish band Beoga, from the remaining tour dates.
Macklemore was removed from the remaining US dates after making comments in support of Palestinians during a performance earlier this month.
Sheeran has said the decision was made by the tour promoter and venue owners, rather than by him personally.
Following his removal, Macklemore announced that he would donate his US$1 million (RM4.2 million) net earnings from the Loop Tour to six organisations supporting Palestinians.
d8eba64a26fa3da1: WASHINGTON: The US approved a potential US$2.68 billion sale of air defence equipment to Ukraine on Friday, after Kyiv made repeated pleas for support to fend off Russian attacks.

The State Department said in a congressional notification that it made "a determination approving a possible Foreign Military Sale to the Government of Ukraine" for buying air defence development upgrades and related equipment and services.
Kyiv has requested to buy equipment including multiple types of missiles, launchers, counter-drone radars and trailers, according to the state department.
The proposed sale is subject to congressional review.

"If the proposed purchase is concluded, Ukraine would finance it using a combination of European contributions and US Foreign Military Financing appropriated during the prior administration," the state department said.
"The estimated total cost is US$2.68 billion."
Ukraine's capital Kyiv has seen a surge in Russian attacks, which its air defences have struggled to repel due to ammunition shortages.
931e055ff51bca09: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Airlines dinobatkan sebagai Kakitangan Syarikat Penerbangan Terbaik di Asia pada Anugerah Syarikat Penerbangan Dunia Skytrax 2026.
Manakala kru kabinnya mendapat tempat ketiga dalam kategori Kru Kabin Syarikat Penerbangan Terbaik Dunia, iaitu meningkat lima tempat daripada tempat kelapan pada 2025.

Syarikat penerbangan itu turut naik enam anak tangga ke tempat ke-21 dalam kategori Syarikat Penerbangan Terbaik Dunia, sekali gus menandakan kemajuan dalam transformasinya yang disokong oleh pelaburan berterusan merentasi sumber manusia, produk, armada, rangkaian dan tawaran kepada pelanggannya.
Malaysia Airlines juga berjaya mengukuhkan kedudukannya dalam beberapa kategori lain pada anugerah tahun ini.

Syarikat penerbangan itu naik dari tempat keenam ke tempat kedua dalam kategori Perkhidmatan Lapangan Terbang Terbaik Dunia, selain membuat penampilan sulungnya di tempat ke-18 dalam kategori Syarikat Penerbangan Kelas Perniagaan Terbaik Dunia.

Ia turut naik ke tempat ke-12 dalam Syarikat Penerbangan Kelas Ekonomi Terbaik Dunia, meningkat daripada tempat ke-16 pada 2025, dan naik ke tempat ke-11 dalam Syarikat Penerbangan Paling Bersih Dunia daripada tempat ke-12 sebelumnya.
Syarikat penerbangan itu juga mengekalkan kedudukannya dalam kalangan 10 Syarikat Penerbangan Terbaik di Asia, dengan meraih kedudukan ke-10 tahun ini.

Presiden dan Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif Kumpulan Malaysia Aviation Group, Nasaruddin A Bakar berkata: “Pengiktirafan ini mencerminkan usaha kolektif kakitangan kami di lapangan terbang, di atas kapal dan di belakang tabir, yang bekerjasama setiap hari untuk memberikan Hospitaliti Malaysia sepanjang perjalanan pelanggan.

"Kejayaan ini dicapai selepas bertahun-tahun mendaki kedudukan global secara konsisten, sekali gus satu pencapaian penting bagi syarikat penerbangan kebangsaan ini, selain satu ganjaran atas usaha gigih pasukan kami," katanya dalam kenyataan.
Beliau berkata, semangat perkhidmatan yang mesra, bertimbang rasa dan konsisten adalah perkara yang membezakan pengalaman Malaysia Airlines.

Menurut kenyataan itu, Malaysia Airlines akan terus mempelbagaikan produk dan tawaran perkhidmatan dalam pesawat sambil mengembangkan rangkaiannya bagi menyediakan lebih banyak pilihan serta kesalinghubungan kepada pelanggannya.

“Pembaharuan armada kekal sebagai bahagian penting dalam hal ini, dengan 29 pesawat baharu diterima setakat ini dan merancang untuk menambah armada kepada 117 pesawat moden menjelang 2035, sekali gus menambah kapasiti untuk menyokong pertumbuhan rangkaian.
“Ia juga disokong dengan tumpuan berterusan terhadap prestasi operasi, dengan prestasi tepat pada masanya purata 91.38% setakat tahun ini, yang secara konsisten melebihi sasaran,” katanya.

Perkembangan ini merupakan sebahagian daripada pelan perniagaan jangka panjang MAG 3.0, dengan sasaran untuk menjadikan Malaysia Airlines sebagai antara 10 syarikat penerbangan global teratas menjelang 2030.
27db4aec75aa21a0: PETALING JAYA: The relationship among unity government components remains good despite the conditional pardon granted to former prime minister Najib Razak, says deputy prime minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
The Umno president said the parties in Putrajaya remain professional in managing the government's affairs with Cabinet decisions made collectively.
"The relationship is good. Although we're politicians, in managing government matters, we act professionally," Bernama quoted him as saying.
Yesterday, the Yang di-Pertuan Agong decided to allow Najib to serve the remainder of his six-year jail sentence in the SRC International case at home provided he pays his RM50 million fine.
Zahid reiterated that the king's decision, following a Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting, was lawful and constitutional.
He warned others against questioning the royal prerogative.
Umno had welcomed Najib’s conditional pardon and launched a fund to help settle his RM50 million fine to allow him to serve his remaining jail term under house arrest.
However, Pakatan Harapan's presidential council said no one was above the law and those convicted of offences should serve their sentences in accordance with the law and the Federal Constitution.
In rebuttal, Umno information chief Azalina Othman Said reminded PH that pardons are lawful as they are provided for under the Federal Constitution, the supreme law of the country.
72914d8a3ba71aea: KUANTAN, Sept 19 — A mother has claimed that her 14-year-old son and another Form Two student were assaulted by five students at a religious school hostel in Bukit Ibam, Rompin, resulting in injuries to various parts of their bodies.

Siti Rohani Yusof, 40, said the first incident occurred at about midnight on Sept 12 when the two students were called into a hostel room, had their heads covered and were allegedly beaten, with her son assaulted for about two hours and his friend for about two and a half hours.
“My son did not dare to tell anyone after the incident for fear of being beaten again. Only on Tuesday did he inform the warden and teachers about what happened.
“He also pleaded to sleep at the warden’s house as he was afraid the incident would recur, but was not allowed to,” she said when met here today.
She said her son was allegedly assaulted again on Sept 15 by the same students using a broomstick, with one holding the stick while another kicked him.
She said her son then contacted his father, who informed the warden, before she went to the school the following day.
She said the senior students allegedly kicked, pinched, slapped and punched her son, besides hitting him with a broomstick.
Her son was later taken to Muadzam Shah Hospital for a medical examination, including X-rays, after a police report was lodged at the Muadzam Shah Police Station.
Siti Rohani said she had also requested police to investigate the hostel management, including the school and warden’s actions in handling the incident.

“I want this matter to be investigated transparently and for the relevant authorities to take the initiative to prevent such incidents from happening again, as well as ensuring the safety and welfare of students in the hostel are guaranteed,” she said.

She also claimed that after the matter was shared in the school’s boys’ hostel (Aspura) parents’ group, more students came forward to share their experiences, and she understood that about 16 students had been victims of similar incidents.
Siti Rohani said she had decided to transfer her son to another school due to concerns over his safety.

Meanwhile, Rompin police chief Supt Sharif Shai Sharif Mondoi confirmed that police had received a report regarding a fight involving two Form Two students at a boys’ hostel of a religious school in Bukit Ibam.

He said preliminary investigations found that the incident occurred at about 12.01 am on Sept 12 after both victims were called to a hostel room by five male students, comprising three Form Five students and two Form Four students.

“The cause of the incident was that the first victim skipped religious lectures, while the second victim was complicit with the first. Both victims were beaten by all the suspects,” he said in a statement today.
Sharif Shai said the first victim suffered injuries to both arms, while the second victim sustained injuries to his body.
He added that all five suspects were detained before being released on police bail, with the case being investigated under Section 147 of the Penal Code. — Bernama
31c9ca5d81e61074: BATU KAWAN: Fourteen of the 20 banking institutions providing hire-purchase financing had begun offering customers the reducing balance method as of Sept 18, said Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali.
He said the remaining six banking institutions were expected to complete the transition to the new method by Dec 31 at the latest, following engagement sessions with the banks.

"In total, there are 429 entities, comprising banking institutions and hire-purchase providers, registered with the Association of Hire Purchase Companies Malaysia," he told reporters at the closing ceremony of the Consumer Festival (CONFEST) 2026 at Batu Kawan Stadium here today.
Armizan added that the ministry had set a target for 80 per cent of hire-purchase providers to offer financing in compliance with the Hire-Purchase (Amendment) Act 2026 by the end of this year.
He said hire-purchase providers that were not yet fully prepared had been granted a grace period until March 31, 2027, with full compliance required from April 1 next year.
He also said the amendments to the Act, which took effect on June 1, introduced the reducing balance method and effective interest rate, replacing the flat interest rate and "Rule of 78" method.
"Under this method, interest is calculated based on the current loan balance, making early loan settlement more transparent for consumers," he said.
CONFEST 2026, themed "Suara Kita: Kuasa Kita", is organised by the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living from Sept 17 to 20.
The 2026 National Consumer Day celebration aims to raise public awareness of consumer rights, protection and responsibilities.

The programme brings together consumer advocacy groups, government agencies and non-governmental organisations through a range of activities, including consumer-related competitions, a Fun Walk, a Fun Run and booths hosted by the ministry's agencies and strategic partners.
241504c69330ec03: TAWAU: A 19-year-old woman was raped by her neighbour, whom she had allowed into her home to help repair her mobile phone.

District police chief Assistant Commissioner Rosdi Mat Jusoh said police received a report from the victim, who alleged that she was raped by a suspect known to her at a People's Housing Project here last Tuesday.

Rosdi said the 26-year-old man, who works as a barber, was arrested by a team of police officers from the Tawau district police headquarters Criminal Investigation Division at his home about 10pm on Thursday.
Preliminary investigations found that the incident was believed to have occurred after the victim allowed the suspect into her home to help repair her mobile phone.
"The suspect is then believed to have taken the victim to a room before committing the alleged offence," he said in a statement today.
The suspect has been remanded for seven days until Sept 25.
5edf14934bac0095: COPENHAGEN: Denmark on Saturday hailed a "binding" deal announced by US President Donald Trump to give Washington "permanent control" over Greenland's security and bar Russian and Chinese bases from the Arctic territory.

Since returning to the White House in January 2025, Trump has repeatedly insisted that Washington needed to control Greenland for strategic reasons, alarming Nato ally Denmark and sparking fierce pushback from the alliance.
Denmark and Greenland – an autonomous Danish territory – both hailed the deal and said they would sign it on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York next week.
Danish foreign minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen said Saturday that the potential signing meant "next week could be a good week".
"A long period of uncertainty will hopefully be replaced by a binding agreement that strengthens security in the Arctic and North Atlantic," the foreign minister said in a social media post.
He added that the deal, which he said respected Denmark's "red lines", was "important" in light of a changed security situation.
But the terms of the deal are uncertain, and Denmark maintains its sovereignty remains intact.
'Permanent control'

In a statement, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen described the deal as "an agreement which at the same time recognises the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom and the Greenlandic people's right to self-determination".

"I am pleased to announce that the United States of America has entered into an Agreement with The Kingdom of Denmark, and Greenland, that gives the United States permanent control over security, and all other needs, in Greenland," Trump said on his Truth Social network.
"From now on, no US adversary can EVER have a base in Greenland, have a military presence in Greenland, or make sensitive investments in Greenland, without our express written approval."
The 80-year-old said it was an "'Infinite Life' Agreement, there is no end!" and said Washington would immediately start building up a large military presence in the territory.

Trump has repeatedly warned about Russia and China trying to establish a foothold in Greenland as a strategic battle for supremacy in a warming Arctic unfolds, and the State Department left no doubt that they would not be allowed to do so.

"This agreement guarantees that China and Russia cannot have a base in Greenland, they cannot send troops to Greenland, and the necessary mechanisms are in place to prevent investment in sensitive sectors," a state department official said.
At the Davos economic forum this past January, Trump reached a purported deal with Nato secretary general Mark Rutte over the future of Greenland, the terms of which have remained vague.
Frederiksen said Friday she was "pleased that there is a prospect of a good agreement for Greenland, the Kingdom of Denmark and the United States," adding that it was "good for Nato and Europe."
Greenland Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen said the deal with the US "strengthens" the territory's security.
Nato tensions
Trump gave no details about how the deal would work, and it was not clear if it was linked to or substantially different from the Rutte deal.

But several media outlets have reported that the United States wants to open three new military bases in southern Greenland, in addition to the Pituffik base it already has in the north of the territory.
A 1951 defence pact, updated in 2004, already allows Washington to ramp up troop deployments and military installations on the island provided it informs Denmark and Greenland in advance.
At the height of the crisis, Trump would not rule out using force to seize the territory of 57,000 inhabitants, sowing anxiety within the EU and Nato.
Since then, tensions have cooled somewhat, and in an apparent move to assuage Trump, Nato launched a new mission to bolster security in the Arctic.
becb8c098e84c8f4: KUALA LUMPUR: Sebanyak 17 kawasan di seluruh negara mencatatkan bacaan indeks pencemar udara (IPU) pada tahap tidak sihat setakat 4 petang ini.

Berdasarkan data Sistem Pengurusan Indeks Pencemaran Udara Malaysia (APIMS), Sarawak merekodkan tujuh kawasan dengan bacaan tidak sihat iaitu IPD Serian (178), Kuching (171), Sri Aman (168), Samarahan (164), Sibu (157), Sarikei (152) dan Bintulu (106).
Di Johor, tiga kawasan merekodkan bacaan tidak sihat iaitu Larkin (158) , Pasir Gudang (155) dan Tangkak (102), diikuti Kuala Lumpur dengan Cheras (149) dan Batu Muda (121).
Seri Manjung, Perak mencatatkan bacaan 159, manakala Shah Alam, Selangor merekodkan 152.
Putrajaya (121), Nilai, Negeri Sembilan (111) dan Bukit Rambai, Melaka (108) turut berada pada tahap tidak sihat.
Sementara itu, sebanyak 38 kawasan lain mencatatkan bacaan pada tahap sederhana, manakala 12 kawasan merekodkan kualiti udara baik.
Bacaan IPU sifar hingga 50 menunjukkan kualiti udara baik, 51 hingga 100 (sederhana), 101 hingga 200 (tidak sihat), 201 hingga 300 (sangat tidak sihat) dan 301 ke atas (berbahaya).
49ba75885b747bca: LONDON: British military sites were targeted by drones more than 300 times over the past year, according to figures published Saturday by UK media.
The Independent newspaper said 340 security incidents involving drones were recorded over or near British defence sites in the 12 months to August 2026.
That compared with 250 incidents in 2025 and 126 the previous year.

Britain's defence ministry did not disclose who was behind the drone activity, but the figures come as European countries warn of an increase in suspected Russian hybrid operations on their territory.
In a statement to AFP, armed forces minister Louise Sandher-Jones said the government was "taking the threat posed by hostile drones to Defence sites extremely seriously".
She said the increase partly reflected improved monitoring and reporting following the creation in February of restricted airspace zones over 44 strategic military sites.

"The UK and its allies remain vigilant against potential threats, and adversaries should be in no doubt about this government's resolve to stand against aggression towards the UK and our allies," a ministry spokesperson added.
The figures were published a day after Russia summoned the UK's charge d'affaires over what Moscow called an "escalation" in arms supplies to Ukraine.
Russia warned that any British military facilities in Ukraine used to launch strikes on Russian territory would be considered "legitimate targets".
ef486e74b4763d91: PETALING JAYA: Persatuan Perubatan Malaysia (MMA) menggesa pihak berkuasa kesihatan memperketat dan mempertingkat penguatkuasaan secara berterusan serta berasaskan risikan terhadap klinik haram dan ubat tidak berdaftar susulan beberapa penemuan kegiatan itu sepanjang tahun ini.

Presiden, Dr L Sivanaesan, berkata tindakan menutup premis terbabit tidak seharusnya menjadi penamat kepada operasi penguatkuasaan kerana pihak yang menjalankannya boleh berpindah dan membuka operasi baharu di lokasi lain.

Beliau berkata, pihak berkuasa kesihatan perlu memperkukuh pemeriksaan bersepadu terhadap premis disyaki menjalankan kegiatan haram, selain pemeriksaan susulan secara berkala terhadap lokasi yang pernah dikenakan tindakan.
"Penguatkuasaan mesti turut menjejaki rantaian bekalan, termasuk bagaimana ubat tidak berdaftar dibawa masuk ke negara ini dan pihak yang sengaja memudahkan pengedarannya.
"Pemeriksaan di pintu masuk negara juga perlu diperketat bagi menghalang ubat tidak berdaftar memasuki Malaysia," katanya dalam kenyataan.
Gesaan itu dibuat selepas Kementerian Kesihatan (KKM) mengesan empat premis di Kuala Lumpur yang menjual dan menyimpan ubat tidak berdaftar, termasuk dua dipercayai beroperasi sebagai klinik haram.
Premis itu dipercayai didalangi warga asing.
Menurut Jabatan Kesihatan Wilayah Persekutuan Kuala Lumpur dan Putrajaya, premis terbabit berselindung di sebalik perniagaan tekstil dan agensi pelancongan, lapor The Star.
Namun, pemeriksaan pihak berkuasa kesihatan menemukan peralatan untuk memeriksa tekanan darah dan paras gula, selain ubat tidak diluluskan KKM.
Sivanaesan mempersoalkan sama ada penguatkuasaan sedia ada dilaksanakan secara konsisten dan cukup untuk menghalang kegiatan sama daripada kembali beroperasi di lokasi lain.

Beliau berkata, penggunaan ubat tidak berdaftar, antibiotik dan peralatan perubatan oleh individu tidak berkelayakan atau tidak berdaftar bukan saja melanggar peraturan, malah membawa risiko serius kepada keselamatan pesakit dan kesihatan awam.
Katanya, penggunaan antibiotik secara tidak wajar turut membimbangkan kerana ia boleh menyumbang kepada kerintangan antimikrob, yang akhirnya mengancam masyarakat secara lebih meluas.

"Ini adalah isu keselamatan pesakit. Perkhidmatan kesihatan mesti diberikan oleh pengamal berkelayakan dan berdaftar, di premis kesihatan berdaftar dengan pihak berkuasa berkaitan, serta hanya menggunakan ubat dan peralatan perubatan diluluskan dalam rawatan pesakit," katanya.
2ae3bc05da5ba741: TAIPEI: Taiwanese actor and basketball personality Blackie Chen has opened up about his "brush with death" after suffering a heart attack on Sept 15, revealing that years of chronic sleep deprivation may have contributed to the medical emergency.

According to a recent new report, the 49-year-old was transferred from the intensive care unit to a general ward on Sept 17 and shared details of the frightening experience on Instagram. Chen said he was playing basketball when he suddenly felt a heavy tightness in his chest.
"It felt like a huge rock was pressing down on [my chest]. I couldn't catch my breath, and my back hurt terribly," he recalled, saying he initially thought he was simply exhausted.

He went to the emergency department at Chung Shan Hospital, where an ECG immediately raised concerns. "When the emergency room nurses saw the ECG results, I could feel the entire atmosphere in the ER change," he said.

Chen was then transferred by ambulance to National Taiwan University Hospital, where doctors performed a cardiac catheterisation and inserted a stent. The entire process, from his arrival at hospital to completion of the procedure, took about 90 minutes. His doctor diagnosed him with an acute myocardial infarction after finding a completely blocked blood vessel.

The incident came as a shock because Chen does not smoke or drink and exercises regularly. However, he admitted to one unhealthy habit: chronic lack of sleep. Since founding the professional basketball league P. League+ in 2020, he had sometimes slept only three to four hours a night while balancing work and family commitments.

"I thought I was made of iron and could handle it," Chen said, recalling how he would sometimes reply to messages at 2am before waking at 6am to get his 11-year-old twin sons, River and Ryan, ready for school. His doctor told him the prolonged sleep deprivation "could have been the most important contributing factor" to his heart attack.

Chen said long-term sleep deprivation can affect cardiovascular health by raising blood pressure, contributing to inflammation and disrupting the autonomic nervous system. "Even if you don't smoke or drink, your heart can still be overworked," he wrote.

Thanking his wife, singer Christine Fan, along with family and friends for supporting him, Chen urged others not to ignore signs of exhaustion. "Being tired is your body crying out for help. Don't wait until you're in the ICU before you listen," he wrote.

He also encouraged people over 40 to undergo annual health screenings and monitor their blood pressure, cholesterol and blood sugar. "Getting six to eight hours of sleep isn't being lazy. It's taking care of your heart."

Chen added: "You can work hard. The basketball game can wait. But when it comes to your health, there is no overtime." He vowed to rest and take better care of himself, saying, "When I'm healthy again, I'll see you on the basketball court."
d27c2c485f73d882: PETALING JAYA: The Malaysian Medical Association has called for tougher, sustained, intelligence-led enforcement by health authorities on illegal clinics and unregistered medicine after repeated discoveries within this year alone.
MMA president Dr L Sivanaesan said simply closing down illegal clinics should not mark the end of enforcement measures as the culprits could reopen elsewhere.
Sivanaesan called for coordinated inspections of suspected premises and regular follow-up inspections of locations previously found operating illegally.
"Enforcement must also follow the supply chain, including how unregistered medicines are brought into the country, and those who knowingly facilitate their distribution.
"There must also be stricter checks at the country's entry points to prevent unregistered medicines from entering Malaysia in the first place," he said in a statement.
This comes after the health ministry discovered four premises in Kuala Lumpur selling and storing unregistered medicines, two of which were allegedly illegal clinics.
They were believed to have been run by foreigners.
The Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya health department said the premises operated under the guise of selling textiles and running travel agencies, The Star reported.
However, inspections by the health authorities led to the discovery of blood pressure and blood sugar testing equipment and medicines that had not been approved by the ministry.
Sivanaesan questioned whether existing enforcement was sustained long enough to prevent such operations from resurfacing elsewhere.
He warned that the use of unregistered medicines, antibiotics and medical equipment by unqualified or unregistered persons poses a serious risk to patients and public health.
He also warned that the inappropriate use of antibiotics was especially concerning as it can contribute to antimicrobial resistance, which threatens the wider population.

"This is first and foremost a patient safety issue. Healthcare must be provided by qualified and registered professionals, at healthcare premises registered with the relevant authorities, with only approved medicines and medical equipment used in the treatment of patients," he said.
c23df549d0f36b71: KUCHING, Sept 19 — Sarawak and Penang will receive greater focus under the government’s efforts to improve Malaysia’s fertility rate and address the country’s low birth rate, said Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri.
She said the ministry planned to place greater emphasis on fertility-related programmes next year, including measures to support couples facing difficulties conceiving.
“Fertility programmes are important because our population is still low and we want to increase it. So we have also proposed programmes related to fertility.

“Sarawak and Penang are among the states that need to be given focus because we want to increase the birth rate,” she told reporters after launching the Program Perantisan Kepimpinan Wanita (Perantis) — Program Pembinaan Kepimpinan dan Keusahawanan Wanita Dayak (Pendaya) 2.0 initiative at Dayak Chamber Tower here today.

Nancy said the ministry’s efforts would include programmes to assist couples facing difficulties having children, including initiatives under the National Population and Family Development Board (LPPKN), such as in-vitro fertilisation (IVF).
She said while such programmes were already being implemented, the ministry intended to give them greater emphasis next year as part of efforts to encourage more young people to have children.
“For us, our focus is more on programmes that can encourage them to have children. Our population needs to increase in this country,” she said.
Nancy said proposals for fertility-related programmes had been included in the ministry’s budget submission, although the final allocation would depend on approval.
She added that studies had also been conducted on fertility rates to support efforts to formulate measures to increase birth rates in Malaysia.
However, she said the figures and findings from the studies would be shared at a later date. — The Borneo Post
8e1fa382266683e7: ROME, Sept 19 — Italian football is mourning the death of former international and Inter Milan great Sandro Mazzola at the age of 83, German Press Agency (dpa) reported, citing his former club on Saturday.
Mazzola spent his entire 17-year professional career with Inter, becoming one of the most influential players in the club’s history.
“Sandro Mazzola was one of the greatest footballers in history,” the club said in a tribute. “He had one shirt for his whole life.”
The attacking midfielder scored 158 goals in 565 competitive appearances for Inter, winning four Italian league titles and two European Cups.
Mazzola scored twice as Inter beat Real Madrid 3-1 in the 1964 European Cup final to win the trophy for the first time. The Italian side successfully defended the title the following year.
Mazzola also enjoyed success with Italy, winning the 1968 European Championship and finishing as runners-up at the 1970 World Cup.
Football also played a defining and tragic role in Mazzola’s childhood.
His father, Valentino Mazzola, was captain of the legendary “Grande Torino” team that dominated Italian football in the 1940s, winning five consecutive league titles.
Valentino Mazzola was killed along with almost the entire Torino team in the Superga air disaster on May 4, 1949.
Sandro Mazzola was 6 years old at the time. — Bernama-dpa
c9d221c37da799e1: JAKARTA: Indonesia has accepted Malaysia's offer to assist in tackling forest and land fires in Kalimantan that have caused transboundary haze affecting the neighbouring countries.
Deputy prime minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said Indonesian president Prabowo Subianto gave his approval during their meeting at Istana Hambalang.

“President Prabowo welcomed the offer, meaning he has given approval for Malaysia to join efforts to address the haze and fires in Kalimantan,” Zahid, who is on a working visit to Jakarta, told a press conference today.

The assistance includes deployment of a Bombardier CL-415MP aircraft, three helicopters, and 52 officers and personnel from the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) and the Royal Malaysian Air Force.

Zahid, who is also the chairman of the Central Disaster Management Committee, said foreign minister Mohamad Hasan had been tasked with coordinating assistance with Nadma, MMEA, the Malaysian meteorological department, the fire and rescue department and other agencies.
He said the assistance was not merely a short-term measure to put out the fires, as both countries had also discussed and agreed on longer-term measures to prevent haze from recurring.

Zahid said Prabowo informed him during the meeting that there were still 1,426 hotspots in Kalimantan, while the Indonesian government had taken legal action against 95 companies involved in open burning in the Borneo region.
Asked if any Malaysian companies were among the 95, he said no such information had been provided so far, although the Indonesian authorities were looking into possible Malaysian involvement.
f394b2cc3e282d50: JAKARTA, Sept 19 — Relations among the parties that make up the unity government remain good following the Pardons Board’s decision involving former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also Umno president, said that in managing government affairs, all parties continue to act professionally, with Cabinet decisions being made collectively.

“The relationship remains good and, although we are politicians, when it comes to managing government affairs, we act professionally, and there is no problem because all decisions by the Cabinet are made collectively.

“In terms of personal relations, Alhamdulillah, they remain good so far. As members of the unity government, we will continue to uphold the principles of discipline as long as we are in the unity government,” he told a media conference today.

Yesterday, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, granted former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak a conditional pardon, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to the payment of a RM50 million fine.

The Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) of the Prime Minister’s Department said the order was decided at the 64th Meeting of the Pardons Board for the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur, Labuan and Putrajaya held at Istana Negara.

Ahmad Zahid, who is also Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman, said the decision of the Pardons Board regarding Najib, which received the consent of His Majesty, was bound by provisions of the Federal Constitution.

“What was decided by the Pardons Board, and received the consent of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, is a decision bound by several clauses in the Malaysian Constitution, and His Majesty would certainly have taken into consideration that legal provisions serve as the basis for the pardon decision.

“So, if any party disputes the King’s decision, it means that it is not in line with the provisions enshrined in the Constitution. Umno and BN themselves are of the view that the law must be obeyed. That position is clear, as reflected in statements I made previously,” he added. — Bernama
421de6f9e5769ef8: BATU GAJAH: Police have yet to confirm whether a fatal accident involving 12 motorcycles that claimed three lives and injured nine others along Jalan Jelapang-Ampang here today was caused by an illegal street race.

Perak deputy police chief Deputy Commissioner Mohammad Azlin Sadari said this could only be confirmed after police recorded statements from the victims who are currently receiving treatment at hospital.

He said preliminary investigations showed that a separate accident involving a car had occurred earlier at the same location, before the vehicle was hit by a group of motorcyclists due to poor lighting conditions.
"Preliminary investigations showed that a car was involved in an accident, causing the vehicle to remain on the main road.
"Poor lighting conditions are believed to have caused a group of motorcyclists to crash into the car.

"Whether they were racing at the time of the incident, we are unable to confirm yet," he said after launching the Amanita Adopted Park Launching Ceremony and Perak Police Chief's Town Hall Discussion Session here today.
In the accident, three motorcyclists were killed while nine others were injured.
Azlin said preliminary investigations confirmed that the group of motorcyclists comprised those aged between 19 and 25.
He said they knew one another and were on their way home after gathering near a convenience store in Meru Raya.

In a related development, Azlin said the Perak Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department had conducted 809 operations this year, including 209 operations around Ipoh, to curb street racing and road hooliganism.
He said the crash site was not, however, identified as a preferred location or "hot spot" for road hooligans.
58b6d9a95ebc2297: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 19 — DAP central executive committee (CEC) members gathered at the party’s national headquarters in Pudu this afternoon for an emergency meeting following the conditional pardon granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
The meeting, which will determine the party’s official position and next steps following yesterday’s decision, began at 3.30pm.
DAP national chairman Gobind Singh Deo was among the earliest to arrive, at 2.40pm, followed by secretary-general Anthony Loke at around 3pm.
DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke arrives at DAP headquarters in Kuala Lumpur September 19, 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif

Other prominent party leaders attending the meeting include Teo Nie Ching, a national vice-chairman and DAP Women’s chief; national deputy chairman Nga Kor Ming; party adviser Lim Guan Eng; national treasurer Ngeh Koo Ham; and Hannah Yeoh.
Last night, Loke said the CEC would determine the party’s official response to the conditional pardon granted to Najib.
DAP national deputy chairman Nga Kor Ming arrives at DAP headquarters in Kuala Lumpur September 19, 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif

The Pardons Board announced yesterday that His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, had consented to allow Najib to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to the payment of a RM50 million fine.

The emergency meeting comes just over a month after DAP delegates voted at the party’s August 16 conference to remain in Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s unity government until the end of the current parliamentary term.
Hannah Yeoh arrives at DAP headquarters in Kuala Lumpur September 19, 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
A total of 1,857 delegates, or about 88 per cent of those who cast valid votes, backed remaining in the government, while 242 voted to leave.
DAP has been a longstanding political ally of Anwar and was a key component of the Pakatan Rakyat coalition before becoming part of its successor, Pakatan Harapan.
d015998076111cd0: ROMPIN: Two religious school students were assaulted by five senior students at a hostel here on Sept 12, after one of them allegedly skipped a religious class, police said.
Rompin deputy district police chief Deputy Superintendent Mohamad Zamri Mohamad Zaber said the two Form Two students were called into a room by their seniors around midnight before being beaten.
"They went to the hostel room, where both victims were beaten by five suspects comprising three Form Five and two Form Four students.

"The attack stemmed from one of the victims skipping a religious class, while the other was claimed to be conspiring with him. The victims suffered injuries to their arms and bodies," he said in a statement today.
Zamri said the victims' parents lodged separate police reports at 1pm on Sept 17, alleging that their children had been beaten by the five male students.
He said police arrested all five suspects for questioning on the same day before releasing them on police bail.
The case is being investigated under Section 147 of the Penal Code for rioting, which carries a maximum jail term of two years, a fine, or both upon conviction.

Earlier, the mother of one of the victims, Siti Rohani Yusof, claimed the incident had left her family traumatised after the suspects allegedly hit her son with a broomstick and threatened him with a penknife.
She also claimed the school had been slow to take action, prompting her to lodge a police report and transfer her son out of the school.
fb9210366a835b7d: Twenty years ago, even Madonna faced radio blacklisting for being overtly political. But in our age of streaming, there’s less excuse for not speaking out It must have come as a surprise to Ed Sheeran when all of his support acts withdrew from the remainder of the US leg of his tour. The American rapper Macklemore had triggered the walkout when he gave an impassioned speech calling for a “free Palestine” on stage and was dropped for doing so. The decision by the remaining acts to drop out in solidarity exposed a deep divide in the modern music industry. Some artists still insist on keeping politics out of music, while others expect music to speak to our perilous times. After he was dropped, Macklemore wrote that Sheeran’s “typical apolitical stance was being challenged in a way it never had been before”, to which Sheeran responded: “I am not complicit” and “those who come to my shows do not expect a political forum”. Jason Okundaye is an assistant Opinion editor at the Guardian Continue reading...
ea408b459e5434b5: SEBERANG PERAI: Empat belas daripada 20 bank di negara ini telah mula menawarkan kaedah baki berkurangan bagi pelanggan pinjaman sewa beli, selaras dengan pindaan Akta Sewa Beli.

Menteri Perdagangan Dalam Negeri dan Kos Sara Hidup Armizan Mohd Ali berkata, baki enam bank lagi komited memuktamadkan peralihan daripada kaedah kadar rata yang lama, serta kiraan 'Rule of 78' kepada kaedah baki berkurangan menjelang 31 Dis ini.
Tambahnya, 80% daripada 429 penyedia perkhidmatan sewa beli yang berdaftar di bawah Persatuan Syarikat Sewa Beli Malaysia sedang beralih kepada kaedah baki berkurangan dan kadar faedah efektif.
"Baki 20% penyedia perkhidmatan perlu selesaikan peralihan ini dalam tempoh penangguhan yang diberikan, iaitu selewat-lewatnya pada 31 Mac 2027.

"Semua penyedia kemudahan sewa beli diwajibkan kuat kuasa undang-undang baharu ini di bawah Akta Sewa Beli yang telah dipinda," katanya pada sidang media sempena Festival Pengguna 2026 di Stadium Batu Kawan hari ini.
Pindaan tersebut memansuhkan kaedah 'Rule of 78' bagi pengiraan penyelesaian awal, selain menstruktur semula kadar faedah tetap bagi sewa beli.
'Rule of 78' merupakan kaedah pengiraan untuk menentukan rebat faedah bagi penyelesaian awal pinjaman sewa beli, iaitu sebahagian besar komponen faedah diperuntukkan pada fasa awal ansuran pinjaman.
Situasi ini menyebabkan peminjam yang ingin membuat penyelesaian awal perlu menanggung baki tertunggak yang tinggi dan tidak mencerminkan kos sebenar pinjaman mereka.
Menerusi kaedah baki berkurangan yang dimandatkan di bawah pindaan akta itu, caj faedah kini akan dikira berasaskan baki prinsipal semasa.
1ccab6f62e090ab5: SINGAPORE, Sept 19 — Haze conditions worsened across parts of South-east Asia since Friday, with Singapore’s air quality slipping back into the unhealthy range as smoke from forest fires in Indonesia drifted towards the city-state.

The 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) in Singapore’s central region reached 107 at 3pm today, up from 102 at 1pm, according to the National Environment Agency (NEA), The Straits Times reported today.
The west region recorded the next-highest reading at 95, while the south registered 79, with both remaining in the moderate range.
The deterioration was more pronounced in the central region, where the hourly PM2.5 reading – a measure of fine particulate matter – jumped from 67 at 11am to 117 at noon before easing to 93 at 3pm.
The NEA advises the public to use hourly PM2.5 readings when deciding on immediate outdoor activities and the 24-hour PSI to plan activities for the day ahead.
The latest deterioration follows an earlier spell of unhealthy air in Singapore this month, with the central-region PSI reaching 101 on September 4.
In its latest advisory, the NEA said smoke plumes from forest fires in Kalimantan had been observed drifting towards Singapore, while some plumes were also seen over southern Sumatra.
Dry conditions are expected to continue over parts of southern Sumatra and Kalimantan, while prevailing winds from the east-south-east or south-east could carry more smoke towards Singapore.
The NEA had forecast the 24-hour PSI to remain in the high-moderate to low-unhealthy range.

The return of unhealthy air this month marks the first such occurrence in Singapore since October 2023, with authorities previously warning of an increased risk of haze between June and October amid warmer and drier conditions associated with El Nino and the Indian Ocean Dipole.
578f87010fe4b613: BATU KAWAN, Sept 19 — Fourteen of the 20 banking institutions providing hire-purchase financing had begun offering customers the reducing balance method as of Sept 18, said Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali.
He said the remaining six banking institutions are expected to complete the transition to the new method by December 31 at the latest, following engagement sessions with the banks.

“In total, there are 429 entities, comprising banking institutions and hire-purchase providers, registered with the Association of Hire Purchase Companies Malaysia (AHPCM),” he told reporters at the closing ceremony of the Consumer Festival (CONFEST) 2026 at Batu Kawan Stadium here today.
Armizan added that the ministry had set a target for 80 per cent of hire-purchase providers to offer financing in compliance with the Hire-Purchase (Amendment) Act 2026 by the end of this year.
He noted that hire-purchase providers that are not yet fully prepared have been granted a grace period until March 31, 2027, with full compliance required from April 1 next year.

According to Armizan, the amendments to the Act that took effect on June 1 introduced the reducing balance method and effective interest rate, replacing the flat interest rate and “Rule of 78” method.
“Under this method, interest is calculated based on the current loan balance, making early loan settlement more transparent for consumers,” he said.
CONFEST 2026, themed “Suara Kita: Kuasa Kita”, is organised by the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) from Sept 17 to 20.
The 2026 National Consumer Day celebration aims to raise public awareness of consumer rights, protection and responsibilities.

The programme brings together consumer advocacy groups, government agencies and non-governmental organisations through a range of activities, including consumer-related competitions, a Fun Walk, a Fun Run and booths hosted by KPDN agencies and strategic partners. — Bernama
d637aaea679d73ac: MELAKA: State Pakatan Harapan is finalising negotiations with parties that share similar aspirations, including Bersatu, to form a PH Plus collaboration to contest the Melaka election.
Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari said the negotiations were being conducted based on decisions made at a meeting of the PH Presidential Council.

"The negotiations also include Bersatu, but any form of cooperation will only be announced after the negotiation process has been completed," he told a press conference after attending the launch of Amanah's election machinery in Duyong here today.
Also present were Amanah president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu, who is also agriculture and food security minister, and Amanah deputy president Datuk Seri Dr Mujahid Yusof Rawa.
Meanwhile, Adly, who is also deputy defence minister, said the distribution of seats within PH among PKR, Amanah and DAP had been finalised, including the allocation of eight seats to Amanah.
Among the state seats Amanah is set to contest are Bukit Katil, Durian Tunggal, Telok Mas and Merlimau.
Asked about the possibility of collaborating with Barisan Nasional, Adly said no negotiations had been held with the party so far.
8d4377a3e57dae66: MILAN: Former Italy forward Sandro Mazzola, who spent all 17 years of his senior career at Inter Milan, has died at the age of 83, the club said on Saturday.

Mazzola, considered a club icon at Inter, scored 158 goals in 565 appearances, helping them win four Serie A titles and two European Cups. He was part of the Italy side that won the Euros in 1968 and reached the World Cup final in Mexico two years later.
