"Sandro Mazzola was one of the greatest footballers in history. Not only in the history of the Nerazzurri," Inter said in a statement on their official website, using a nickname for the team. "He was Inter’s history: he joined the club as a boy and never left it."
Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said Italy had lost one of the most beloved figures in its soccer history.
"He brought joy and passion to generations of Italians, leaving an indelible mark on our nation," she posted on social media.

Mazzola was six years old when his father, Valentino, also an Italian international, died in the Superga air disaster, a plane crash in May 1949 that killed the entire Torino team on their way back from a match in Lisbon.

At 18, Mazzola made his senior debut when Inter fielded their youth side in a match against Juventus, after the Italian federation overturned a decision awarding Inter a 2-0 victory following a pitch invasion by Juventus fans and ordered a replay.
Mazzola, who had been a club mascot at Inter as a child, finished a school exam before travelling to Turin, where he scored Inter's only goal from a penalty in a 9-1 defeat to Juventus.

He quickly became a first-team regular, helping Inter win their first European Cup in 1964 by scoring a brace as they beat Real Madrid 3-1 in the final. He played a key role when Inter won the title again the next season.
Mazzola retired as a player in 1977 and later served as Inter's sporting director. He also became the sporting director of Torino, his father's club.

"The star with the moustache shone on the pitch and still does today. As he often said, he had one final wish: to be remembered as a good man, someone who keeps fighting even when winning is impossible, like in that 9-1," Inter said.
7ec39927b46a0df4: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Medical Association (MMA) has called for tougher enforcement after the latest discovery of suspected illegal clinics and seizure of unregistered medicines and medical equipment.
"What is particularly worrying is that this comes only months after similar illegal clinics were uncovered earlier this year," MMA president Dr L. Sivanaesan said in a statement.

He said the use of unregistered medicines, injections, antibiotics and medical equipment by unqualified or unregistered individuals posed a serious risk to patients and public health. It said inappropriate use of antibiotics could also contribute to antimicrobial resistance.

Healthcare must be provided by qualified and registered professionals at premises registered with the relevant authorities, using only approved medicines and medical equipment in treating patients, Dr Sivanaesan said.

The association called for tougher, sustained and intelligence-led enforcement, including coordinated inspections of suspected premises and regular follow-up inspections at locations previously found to be operating illegally.

Dr Sivanaesan said enforcement must also follow the supply chain, including how unregistered medicines are brought into the country and those who knowingly facilitate their distribution. It also called for stricter checks at the country's entry points to prevent unregistered medicines from entering Malaysia.
MMA said stronger action was needed not only against those operating illegal clinics, but also against the networks supplying and facilitating the unlawful activities.

Dr Sivanaesan said the government should also address healthcare access challenges faced by undocumented migrants, as fear of coming into contact with enforcement authorities might discourage some from seeking care at registered healthcare facilities, leaving them vulnerable to illegal providers.

MMA urged the public not to compromise their health to save a small amount of money, saying treatment from unqualified individuals or illegal clinics might appear cheaper but could result in serious health and financial consequences.
In June, the Health Ministry said it would step up enforcement against unlicensed healthcare premises, including those offering aesthetic medical services, following a rise in complaints.
The ministry said it had received more than 1,020 complaints about unlicensed medical facilities since 2021, with the number increasing each year.
"The recurrence raises questions about whether enforcement is sufficiently sustained to prevent such operations from simply resurfacing elsewhere," Dr Sivanaesan said.
a981ec090386714f: KUALA TERENGGANU: The Health Ministry recorded 102 deceased organ donors from January to August this year, up from 89 in 2025, but 12,575 patients remain on the waiting list for new organs as of July.

Deputy director-general of health (Medical) Datuk Dr Azman Yacob said the figures, equivalent to about 1.3 deceased donors per million population, showed that public awareness of organ donation had taken root but remained far from satisfactory.

"Compared to international statistics, countries such as the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Spain and others have higher organ acceptance rates, reaching 20 to 30 per million population," he told reporters after officiating the launch of National Organ Donation Awareness Week (MKPO) 2026 here today.

Speaking on this year's theme, "Warisku, Hormati Ikrarku" (My Heirs, Honour My Pledge), he said MKPO carried the message that a person's wish to donate their organs after death was a humanitarian pledge that deserved to be honoured, with family support and understanding.
Dr Azman said many families were unaware of their loved one's wish to donate, which was among the reasons the number of deceased organ donations remained low and more lives could not be saved.
He said although some 450,000 individuals were registered as organ donors, the number of actual donations remained low as families had the final say on whether donation proceeded after death.

"When the time comes, when a donor falls ill due to an accident, brain death or other causes, they can no longer make the decision. So awareness among family members is crucial to honouring the donor's wishes," he said.
Dr Azman said Terengganu was chosen to host this year's MKPO following encouraging progress in organ and tissue donation across the East Coast states, reflecting growing public awareness.
He said Terengganu recorded seven organ or tissue donation procedures this year, while Pahang and Kelantan each recorded one, their first in a long time.
Meanwhile, Dr Azman said the Health Ministry would continue efforts to increase the number of actual organ donors through various measures.
These include setting up the National Transplant Council as a strategic platform to improve coordination of the country's organ donation and transplantation agenda.

He added that the ministry would also step up engagement with institutions across all religions to help the public better understand organ donation, including the fact that it does not contradict religious requirements.
"Sustained explanation of the legal and religious aspects is crucial, as confusion over these matters can be a factor deterring people from coming forward as organ donors," he said.
402f185caeb12766: BATU KAWAN, Sept 19 — The government aims to finalise the drafting of a new e-commerce Bill this year, said Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali.
He said the ministry had approved the policy decision to repeal the Electronic Commerce Act 2006 and replace it with a new, more comprehensive law.
However, he said the process would require coordination between ministries as well as extensive engagement with stakeholders, including e-commerce platforms, service providers and industry players.

“We know that e-commerce is a broad and comprehensive area, so it requires extensive engagement with stakeholders. We need to examine the matter thoroughly, and I hope it can be finalised,” he told reporters after launching the 2026 Consumer Festival (Confest 2026) at Batu Kawan Stadium here today.

Armizan said two committees had also been established to expedite the drafting of the bill, including to facilitate coordination between the ministry, the Ministry of Communications and the Ministry of Digital.
He said matters currently being fine-tuned included the division of responsibilities among the ministries and relevant agencies, as well as the regulatory mechanisms for e-commerce platforms.
The next stage would also require a regulatory impact assessment (RIA) in collaboration with the Malaysia Productivity Corporation (MPC) before the bill is submitted for further consideration.

Among the proposals being studied is the introduction of a licensing regime for e-commerce platforms, particularly in view of the influx of goods from overseas, consumer safety and the sustainability of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
However, Armizan said regulation must be balanced so as not to hamper the growth of the e-commerce sector, which provides convenience to consumers and serves as a source of income for traders.
“We want more comprehensive and conducive regulation, but at the same time, we do not want to hamper the growth of e-commerce,” he said.

The government had previously expressed its intention to expedite the drafting of the e-commerce Bill to strengthen the regulation and accountability of platforms, sellers and consumers, given that the Electronic Commerce Act 2006 does not provide a comprehensive legal framework to regulate various aspects of e-commerce. — Bernama
0720f7fb7f8da6f3: JAKARTA: Hubungan antara parti menganggotai kerajaan perpaduan kekal baik susulan keputusan lembaga pengampunan melibatkan bekas perdana menteri Najib Razak, kata Timbalan Perdana Menteri Zahid Hamidi.
Beliau yang juga presiden Umno berkata, dalam menguruskan hal ehwal kerajaan semua pihak terus bertindak secara profesional dengan keputusan Jemaah Menteri dibuat secara kolektif.

“Hubungan tetap baik dan biarpun kami ahli-ahli politik, tetapi dalam menguruskan hal ehwal kerajaan, kita bertindak secara profesional, dan itu tidak ada sebarang masalah kerana semua keputusan yang dibuat oleh Jemaah Menteri adalah keputusan yang dibuat secara kolektif.

“Hubungan peribadi setakat ini, Alhamdulillah, cukup baik dan sebagai anggota di dalam kerajaan perpaduan, prinsip ketatasusilaan itu tetap kami jaga selagi kami berada dalam Kerajaan Perpaduan,” katanya pada sidang media hari ini.
Semalam, Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim berkenan memberikan pengampunan bersyarat kepada Najib dengan membenarkan beliau menjalani baki hukuman secara tahanan di rumah hingga 23 Ogos 2028.

Menurut Bahagian Hal Ehwal Undang-undang (BHEUU) Jabatan Perdana Menteri, pengampunan bersyarat itu yang diputuskan Mesyuarat Lembaga Pengampunan Ke-64 bagi Wilayah Persekutuan Kuala Lumpur, Labuan dan Putrajaya di Istana Negara, tertakluk pembayaran denda RM50 juta serta pematuhan syarat ditetapkan.

Zahid yang juga pengerusi Barisan Nasional (BN) berkata, keputusan lembaga pengampunan berhubung Najib diperkenankan Yang di-Pertuan Agong adalah terikat dengan peruntukan dalam Perlembagaan Persekutuan.

“Apa yang diputuskan lembaga pengampunan, yang diputuskan Yang di-Pertuan Agong adalah keputusan yang terikat dengan beberapa klausa di dalam Perlembagaan Malaysia, dan tentunya Tuanku telah mengambil perkiraan bahawa aspek perundangan menjadi panduan terhadap keputusan pengampunan.

“Jika mana-mana pihak yang mempertikaikan keputusan Tuanku Agong, ertinya ia tidak selari dengan perkara-perkara yang termaktub di dalam Perlembagaan, dan Umno serta BN sendiri berpendirian bahawa undang-undang itu harus dipatuhi. Pendirian itu adalah jelas sebagaimana kenyataan-kenyataan yang pernah saya keluarkan sebelum ini,” katanya.
58fffc2eccaa5d38: NEW DELHI: Indians living in Japan are standing by to house the country's athletes at the Asian Games if accommodation shortages continue, officials said Saturday.
Asia's biggest sporting spectacular opens officially in Nagoya and Aichi prefecture on Saturday night, but the build-up to the event has been dogged by problems.

To save money, Japan decided against having an athletes' village, with organisers choosing to put up competitors in a combination of hotel rooms, temporary wooden container-style huts and on a cruise ship.

But many of the 17,000 athletes and officials descending on Japan for the Games have been unhappy with their allocated temporary accommodation, saying rooms have no storage space for kit and the beds are too small.

India, who are sending almost 500 athletes to the Asian Games, have moved some from the huts into hotels and have put in place contingency plans should the shortage of suitable rooms get worse as more competitors and support staff arrive in the coming days.
"We have booked hotels for our athletes here," Sahdev Yadav, India's chef de mission at Asian Games and the Indian Olympic Association (IOA)'s treasurer, told AFP.
"But if the hotel rooms fall short then yes, we have Indian households here on standby to accommodate the athletes.
"They are all more than happy to welcome the stars at their homes."
Reports said the Indian embassy in Japan had helped reach out to around 2,000 families in Nagoya, some of whom are prepared to help.
Organisers said the accommodation was safe, cost-effective and comfortable and Japan should be applauded for trying to do something different. - AFP
438afed02ffcb7a2: PETALING JAYA: Kementerian Dalam Negeri (KDN) masih belum dimaklumkan secara rasmi oleh Lembaga Pengampunan Wilayah Persekutuan berhubung kebenaran Najib Razak menjalani baki hukuman penjara di bawah tahanan rumah jika bekas perdana menteri itu menjelaskan denda RM50 juta.

Menteri Dalam Negeri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail berkata, kementeriannya dan Jabatan Penjara tidak dapat membuat sebarang persiapan yang sewajarnya selagi belum menerima surat serta perincian mengenai pengampunan bersyarat itu.

"Saya masih lagi menunggu pemakluman, biasanya oleh Bahagian Hal Ehwal Undang-Undang (BHEUU) Jabatan Perdana Menteri yang menjadi sekretariat kepada Lembaga Pengampunan," katanya pada sidang media di Kedah.

"Daripada pemakluman itu nanti, barulah kita jelas apakah tindakan selanjutnya yang akan kita ambil, tindakan ke arah melaksanakan keputusan tersebut sesuai dengan peruntukan undang-undang sedia ada."
Beliau bagaimanapun enggan mengulas sama ada kediaman Najib di Taman Duta sesuai dijadikan lokasi tahanan rumah.
Katanya, kementeriannya perlu melihat terlebih dahulu sama ada Lembaga Pengampunan telah menetapkan lokasi khusus atau menyerahkannya kepada budi bicara Jabatan Penjara.

Saifuddin turut menjelaskan bahawa Malaysia belum mempunyai undang-undang khusus berkaitan tahanan rumah, namun menegaskan beliau sedang merangka rang undang-undang (RUU) bagi membolehkan pelaksanaan tahanan rumah, khususnya untuk tahanan reman.
"Saya sudah pun mendapat persetujuan Kabinet secara dasar untuk saya mulakan proses bentangkan Akta Tahanan Rumah di Parlimen.
"Jika rang undang-undang itu diluluskan, kita boleh keluarkan tahanan reman ini di rumah dan kita pakaikan segala peranti moden untuk mengawasi pergerakan mereka sehingga tarikh perbicaraan.
"Itu maksud asal yang kita bincangkan," katanya.
72e93324099e4fc7: PETALING JAYA: The government will provide a one-off RM1,000 Mobility Assistance Allowance to Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) contributors who secure new jobs located more than 100km from their homes.
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said under the Act the allowance would take effect on Oct 1 through amendments to the Employment Insurance System Act 2017.
Among the changes is an increase in the Early Re-employment Allowance from 25 per cent to 50 per cent of the remaining unpaid Job Search Allowance for eligible workers who return to employment early.
"The daily Training Allowance will increase from between RM10 and RM20 to RM30, while the maximum Training Fee covered will rise from RM4,000 to RM7,000.

"This means contributors will receive better support to undergo training, improve their skills and adapt to current job market requirements," Ramanan said at the launch of the three-day Mega iLINDUNGu Festival: Kesuma Bersama Rakyat at Strand Mall here.
Ramanan said under the Act, support and protection provided under the Employment Insurance System (EIS) for each contributor amounted to up to RM25,000.
"However, this is subject to eligibility and the benefits received," he said.
2dad738476f1eddd: KUALA TERENGGANU, Sept 19 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) recorded 102 deceased organ donors from January to August this year.
Deputy Director-General of Health (Medical) Datuk Dr Azman Yacob said this is an increase from the 89 deceased organ donors in 2025, equivalent to roughly 1.3 donors per million population.

He said both figures showed that public awareness of the importance of organ donation had taken root, but was still far from satisfactory, with 12,575 patients still on the waiting list for new organs as of July this year.

“Compared to international statistics, countries such as the UAE (United Arab Emirates), Spain and others have higher organ acceptance rates, reaching 20 to 30 per cent per million population,” he told reporters after officiating the launch of National Organ Donation Awareness Week (MKPO) 2026 here today.

Speaking on this year’s theme, “Warisku, Hormati Ikrarku” (My Heirs, Honour My Pledge), he said MKPO carries the message that a person’s wish to donate organs after death is a humanitarian pledge that deserves to be honoured and affirmed through their family’s support and understanding.
Dr Azman said many families are unaware of their loved one’s wish to donate, which is among the reasons deceased organ donation numbers remain low, and why more lives are not being saved.
He noted that although some 450,000 individuals are registered as organ donors, the number of actual donations remains low, since families have the final say on whether donation proceeds after death.

“When the time comes, when a donor falls ill due to an accident, brain death or other causes, they can no longer make the decision. So awareness among family members is crucial to honouring the donor’s wishes,” he said.

Meanwhile, Dr Azman said Terengganu was chosen to host this year’s MKPO in light of encouraging progress in organ and tissue donation across the East Coast states, reflecting growing public awareness.
He said Terengganu recorded seven organ or tissue donation procedures this year, while Pahang and Kelantan each recorded one, their first in a long time.
Meanwhile, Dr Azman said the Health Ministry will continue to work on increasing the number of actual organ donors through various measures.
This includes setting up the National Transplant Council as a strategic platform to drive better coordination of the country’s organ donation and transplantation agenda.

He added that MOH will also step up engagement with institutions across all religions, helping the public better understand organ donation, including the fact that it does not contradict religious requirements.
“Sustained explanation of the legal and religious aspects is crucial, as confusion over these matters can be a factor deterring people from coming forward as organ donors,” he said. — Bernama
cce15b695548f62a: SINGAPORE, Sept 19 — Two men have been arrested in Singapore after Italian authorities investigating an international online child abuse network passed information to local police.
The Singapore Police Force (SPF) confirmed to The Straits Times today that the men, aged 27 and 33, were arrested for possessing or gaining access to child abuse material.
The SPF said it received information from Italian authorities about an operation targeting a Telegram group that shared such material, and investigations are ongoing.
The police did not disclose the men’s nationalities or whether they are known to each other.

The arrests follow an Italian investigation that led to 17 arrests on September 17, after an undercover officer infiltrated the Telegram network by gaining the trust of its administrators, AFP reported.

The operation, dubbed Fly Trap, uncovered a Telegram community known as New Saga with more than 1,000 users worldwide, while Italian authorities identified 996 accounts linked to 98 countries and shared the information with foreign authorities.
The network was run by four Italians and a Swiss national, with the investigation beginning in 2024 following a tip-off from US Homeland Security Investigations.

In Singapore, anyone convicted of possessing or gaining access to child abuse material while knowing or having reason to believe it is such material can be jailed for up to five years, fined or caned.
659e7aff1bb6ce0d: PETALING JAYA: A parents' group and an academic have criticised the 30% Bumiputera equity condition for tuition centres, calling for the education ministry to drop this requirement for licence renewals in 2027.

The Melaka Action Group for Parents in Education (Magpie) and independent scholar Sharifah Munirah Alatas said the move was unfair to operators who have built their business over years, and fails to actually encourage Bumiputera entrepreneurship.
Sharifah said this policy is absurd and risks racialising the education sector, adding that it only exemplifies how distracted the education ministry is from more pertinent issues.

"This directive is another example of how our government gets bogged down in trivial administrative interventions. It fails to focus on the structural obligations, such as teacher training, administrative bloat, overwork, and other classroom challenges," she said in a Facebook post.
She said the 30% equity condition merely distributes earned benefits to passive groups instead of actually birthing Bumiputera entrepreneurs in the sector.

"Throughout economic history, genuine entrepreneurs have never been the product of affirmative action enforced willy-nilly. Rather, they emerge organically through personal struggle, market discipline, and risk-taking.

"When aspiring entrepreneurs fail, they don’t run to the state for bailouts. Neither should the state offer any. When they fail, they should lick their wounds, pick themselves up, and then try again," she said.
Magpie president Mak Chee Kin said the government should provide financing, training and grants if it wants to boost Bumiputera participation in tuition centres.
"Is it fair to require existing businesses, some of which have operated successfully for decades, to surrender 30% of their ownership simply to continue operating?

"These entrepreneurs invested their own money, took risks, employed teachers, and built their centres from the ground up. They should not be penalised by a policy introduced years after they established their businesses.

"Magpie urges the government to reconsider this policy and, most importantly, protect existing tuition centres that have been operating legally and responsibly for many years," he said in a statement.
Mak also questioned whether the Bumiputera equity rule could be extended to other sectors little by little.

Earlier this week, Petaling Jaya MP Lee Chean Chung said a ministry guideline purportedly stated that tuition centres must have 30% Bumiputera equity in order to have their licences renewed next year.
Lee urged the ministry to explain the basis for the move and to consult operators and give them clear guidance on the implementation of the policy.
3f7ebb8d63862d69: NAGOYA: Japan's hosting of the Asian Games with huts and a cruise ship is an example for other nations if they want to stage major events without breaking the bank, a senior Olympic official said Saturday.
The build-up to Asia's biggest sporting spectacular has been overshadowed by a shortage of accommodation in Nagoya for the more than 17,000 participants.
Some countries have also complained about the quality of the rooms, especially in the shipping container-style huts.
Japanese organisers did not build an athletes' village, as is normally done, in a bid to cut costs.
About 4,000 participants are housed instead on cruise liner Costa Serena, which is sitting in Nagoya's port, with another 2,000 in the wooden huts.
The rest are in hotels in the city and across Aichi prefecture.
Despite complaints from some teams, Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) director general Husain Al-Musallam said Japan should be applauded for trying to do something different.
"Everyone talks about the cost of the Games and how the Games should be managed, and then Japan comes up with a new idea and tries something where there is no athletes' village," he said.
"Because the most important thing we are taking care of as the OCA for the host is what will happen after the closing.
"What's going to happen to your investment after the closing? We don't want Japan to lose their money for nothing."
Al-Musallam said nations with a desire to host major international competitions – not just the Asian Games – should take note.
"What Japan have done here, and Aichi-Nagoya and Olympic Council of Asia, could be the future example for the cost-reduction of multi-sport events such as the Asian Games," he said.
The Games officially open later Saturday. - AFP
7c042e5e4c94bbf7: JAKARTA, Sept 19 — Indonesia has given the green light for Malaysia to assist in tackling forest and land fires in Kalimantan that have caused transboundary haze affecting neighbouring countries, including Malaysia.

Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto gave his approval during their meeting at Istana Hambalang in conjunction with his working visit to Jakarta.
“President Prabowo welcomed the offer, meaning he has given approval for Malaysia to join efforts to address the haze and fires in Kalimantan,” he told a press conference here today.

The assistance includes a Bombardier CL-415MP aircraft, three helicopters, and 52 officers and personnel from the National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA), the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (APMM), and the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF).

Ahmad Zahid, also chairman of the Central Disaster Management Committee, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan was tasked with coordinating assistance with NADMA, APMM, the Malaysian Meteorological Department, RMAF, the Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM), and other relevant agencies.

“Now that approval has been obtained from President Prabowo, coordination at the ministry, department and agency levels must take place. I hope the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, in carrying out this coordination, will ensure that all parties involved in the operation work in a coordinated manner,” he said.

He said the assistance was not merely a short-term measure to put out the fires, as both countries had also discussed and agreed on longer-term measures to prevent haze caused by such fires from recurring.

Ahmad Zahid said Prabowo also informed him during the meeting that there were still 1,426 hotspots in Kalimantan, while the Indonesian government had taken legal action against 95 companies involved in open burning in the Borneo region.

Asked whether any Malaysian companies were among the 95 companies, Ahmad Zahid said no such information had been provided so far, adding that the Indonesian authorities were looking into possible Malaysian involvement.
“The companies are registered as Indonesian companies. In terms of shareholding, however, some of them may have a small proportion of shares owned by Malaysian shareholders,” he said.

He said Malaysia welcomed the measures taken by Indonesia and, as its closest neighbour, would continue to cooperate in tackling fires and transboundary haze, particularly their impact on Sarawak. — Bernama
a71241e1d7090a9d: LUMUT, Sept 19 — The Defence Ministry (Mindef) is in the final stage of shortlisting a surface-to-surface missile system from three countries to replace the system for the Royal Malaysian Navy Littoral Combat Ships (LCS).
Without disclosing the three countries, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said several issues needed to be finalised before a government decision could be made.

“We are at the final stage. We have shortlisted three surface-to-surface missiles from three countries,” he said at a press conference after officiating the launch of the Cyber Force Nucleus Team in conjunction with the 93rd Malaysian Armed Forces Day at the Royal Malaysian Navy Base here today.
In July, Malaysia decided to immediately halt any procurement of new defence equipment or assets from Norway following the country’s decision to revoke the export licence for the LCS missile system.

Meanwhile, commenting on the possibility of Malaysia acquiring the BrahMos air-to-surface missile system from India, he said the matter would be referred to the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) for study.

“If there is a proposal, we will refer it to the RMAF for study, including the implications and integration of the system, as well as upgrading the systems on RMAF defence assets, including the Sukhoi fighter aircraft.
“We will also look at our defence doctrine, because what we currently have has a range of no more than 100 kilometres, while that system has a range of 300 to 400 kilometres,” he said.

Last week, during his visit to New Delhi, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim confirmed that Malaysia was exploring and studying preliminary discussions on acquiring the BrahMos supersonic cruise missile system from India. — Bernama
596b6e8d873630e0: KUANTAN: A businesswoman was left distressed after her 14-year-old son was allegedly assaulted by several senior students using a broomstick at a religious secondary school in Rompin last week.

What upset the 40-year-old was the school's alleged failure to look into the matter despite being alerted by her son, prompting her to take matters into her own hands, including lodging a police report and "rescuing" her son from the school.
Siti Rohani Yusof said the incident had left her family traumatised, particularly her son, while the alleged lack of action by the school, including its principal and hostel warden, came as a shock.

The mother of two said the incident occurred on Sept 12, when five senior students called her son and his friend to their hostel room at about midnight before advising them not to leave the school premises without permission.
"Suddenly, they blindfolded my son and began punching him in the stomach, kicking his back, slapping his face and hitting him with a broomstick.
"They assaulted him for more than an hour. They even threatened to injure him with a penknife and a piece of glass," she told reporters at her house in Bukit Rangin here today.
She said her son informed the school management about the incident, but no action was taken.
Upon learning that the senior students were planning another assault, her son called and informed his father using a public phone on Sept 16.
Siti Rohani said when she contacted the hostel warden, she was told there was no need for her to travel to the school as the matter had been settled.
"I decided to immediately go to the school and, upon reaching the hostel, I was shocked to see my son's body and hands covered in bruises.
"The seniors allegedly involved in the incident were moving around freely.

"I lodged a police report on Sept 17 and took my son to hospital for a check-up. When I shared details about the incident with other parents, I was informed that several children had previously been assaulted by the seniors but the incidents were never disclosed by the school," she said.
Siti Rohani said she was upset that the school, despite being aware of the incident involving its students, had allegedly chosen to conceal the matter.
"My son was forced to treat his own injuries... I am fortunate that my son is still alive.
"Concerned about my son's safety, I told him to pack his belongings on Sept 16 and I am in the process of transferring him to another school," she said.

Meanwhile, Rompin deputy district police chief Deputy Superintendent Mohamad Zamri Mohamad Zaber said police had arrested five students after two victims lodged separate reports at about 1pm on Sept 17.
He said the suspects, comprising three Form Five and two Form Four students, were questioned to assist investigations under Section 147 of the Penal Code for rioting.
The offence carries a maximum two years' imprisonment, a fine, or both, upon conviction.
"Both victims sustained injuries believed to have resulted from the assault. All the suspects have been released on police bail," he said.

907158e6edae446a: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's sepak takraw squad suffered a blow ahead of their campaign at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games after star tekong Noraizat Nordin was ruled out with a training injury.
The Sepaktakraw Federation of Malaysia (STAM) said in a statement that Noraizat was injured during a session on Saturday before medical tests confirmed he could not compete.
STAM has submitted a player replacement request to the Olympic Council of Asia through the Olympic Council of Malaysia, naming Shahalril Aiman Halim to take Noraizat's place in the national squad.
The last-minute swap will test the national team as they target a gold medal at the Games.
STAM said it hopes the replacement process will run smoothly and wished Noraizat a speedy recovery.
The men's team regu campaign begins in Group B against Japan on Sunday, followed by matches against the Philippines on Monday and India on Tuesday.
The semi-finals are set for Thursday, with the final scheduled for Friday.
13b3624f84336ac7: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno is targeting up to RM30 million for the Tabung Solidariti Najib Razak if all of its estimated 3.8 million members nationwide contribute to the fund.
Umno supreme council member Datuk Razlan Rafii said the target was achievable if each member contributed at least RM10.
"Looking at the amount collected so far, we are positive about the support given to the Tabung Solidariti Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
"After this, contributions will be easier once we obtain the bank's QR code, allowing people to use digital platforms to contribute," he said when contacted today.
Razlan said organisers were optimistic that the target could be reached as soon as possible, with no official closing date set for the fund.
Umno launched the fund to help former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak pay a RM50 million fine imposed as a condition of his conditional pardon.

Recalling a similar effort in the past, Razlan said he had previously launched a fund in July 2018 to help pay part of Najib's bail in the case involving alleged misappropriation of SRC International funds.
"Previously, we launched a fund to help with Najib's bail and managed to collect RM500,000 within a short period, thanks to the spirit of party members," he said.
On negative reactions on social media to the latest fund, Razlan claimed the opposition was deliberately generated by certain parties using "cyber armies".
"Many support Najib, but we face challenges when certain parties deliberately campaign to shape public opinion in Malaysia.
"These are all paid bots; it is not a true reflection of Malaysians," he said.
Razlan also urged the public to consider Najib's contributions and services fairly.
"Every leader has their contributions and achievements. The wrongs or mistakes they have made should be balanced against their contributions. That is what is most important," he said.
He also commented on the stance previously taken by some government leaders who had said they were prepared to resign if Najib was granted a pardon.
Razlan said the current situation showed how far the leaders concerned valued their positions over their principles.
"Today, we can see how much they value their positions over their principles," he said.

2e40ee7455e1076d: PUTRAJAYA: Applicants for the new-generation MyKad are allowed to have dyed hair as long as the colour looks natural and is not too prominent.

National Registration Department Identification Card Division director Muhammad Asraf Sukadi said the requirement also took into account an individual's original hair colour, including those with grey hair or who use henna.
He said the department did not require applicants to have black hair, but the colour should closely resemble their natural hair colour and not be excessive.
"We allow hair colours that are close to the original colour. For example, grey hair or hair coloured using henna, as long as it is not too prominent.

"For example, if someone is of Eurasian descent, we allow it, and there is no problem. But it should not be completely blonde. The colour should be more natural," he said during an interview on a programme with radio station Kool FM.

The clarification followed a picture of a new-generation MyKad belonging to a female singer that went viral on social media, prompting discussion over hair colour and several other requirements for identification card photographs.
Meanwhile, he said claims that applicants must wear a black headscarf when having their photograph taken for the new MyKad were inaccurate.
He said the department required applicants wearing headscarves to use dark colours because the background of the MyKad photograph was white.
"We did not say black. We said dark colours because the background is white.
"If they wear a light-coloured headscarf, we will not be able to see it properly in the photograph," he said
472898381edb0c2a: BURSSELS: The EU said on Saturday it regretted Washington's decision to deny visas for the second year running to Palestinian officials seeking to attend the UN General Assembly, urging a rethink.
The US state department said this week it was refusing to grant visas to Palestinian leader Mahmoud Abbas and other members of his delegation ahead of next week's meeting in New York.
"We regret the decision to extend the denial of entry visas for members of the Palestinian delegation for a second year in a row," said Anouar El Anouni, a spokesman for the EU's diplomatic service.
"In light of its existing headquarters agreements with the UN and its obligations as host state, we urge the United States for this decision to be reconsidered."

The administration of US President Donald Trump denied visas for the Palestinian delegation also last year, forcing Abbas, a regular at the UN General Assembly, to address the body of global leadership by video.
The General Assembly voted 152-3 on Thursday for Abbas to be able to appear virtually once again this year.
As it stands, only members of the Palestinian mission to the UN will be able to attend the meeting, which begins Tuesday.

On Friday, UN secretary-general Antonio Guterres also expressed regret at Washington's decision, adding he was concerned about its impact "on the ability of the State of Palestine to participate fully in the work of the UN".
The US and Israel have objected to the Palestinian Authority's historical payments to families of imprisoned or slain Palestinians, including those who carried out attacks against Israelis.
The PA recently reformed this system, allocating welfare payments to families on a needs basis rather than political affiliation or prisoner status.

The state department said Washington also opposed Palestinian "actions to internationalise the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, including through the International Criminal Court (ICC) and International Court of Justice (ICJ), seeking to bypass negotiations through seeking unilateral recognition".
They accused them of "continuing to pay stipends to terrorists and to glorify acts of terrorism and terrorists in public pronouncements and school textbooks".
The US is at odds with the 142 UN member states that recognised a Palestinian state at the UN last year.
The decision to deny Abbas a US entry visa comes as violence by Israeli settlers against Palestinians has escalated in recent months in the West Bank.
7c10017f2ac8f50c: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 19 — The Home Ministry is still waiting for the official written notification of the Pardons Board’s reported decision to place former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak under house arrest before deciding on its next course of action.

Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the ministry and Prisons Department had yet to receive the letter from the Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister’s Department, which serves as the secretariat to the Pardons Board.

“Once we receive the notification, only then will we be clear about what further action we need to take, and the steps towards implementing the decision in accordance with the existing provisions of the law.
“As of now, we have not received anything,” he told reporters in Kulim, Kedah today.
He was visiting the families of four young boys who drowned in Taman Desa Kayangan, Sungai Karangan after trying to retrieve a ball.

Saifuddin said the letter would also clarify whether the Pardons Board had specified the premises where Najib would serve his reported house arrest, or whether the matter had been left to the Prisons Department.

“I need to see the letter first. Currently, Datuk Seri Najib is serving his prison sentence. House arrest means he will not be in prison but at another premises, and there are naturally processes to follow. That is why I said I want to see the letter first,” he said.
He said the ministry would also examine whether the Pardons Board’s decision contained any further instructions or delegated authority to the Prisons Department.

“Based on that letter, we will see whether it is limited to the decision of the Pardons Board, or whether the Board has also given further authority to the Prisons Department. We will examine all of that,” he said.

Saifuddin said Najib was currently still serving his prison sentence, adding that house arrest would mean he was no longer held in prison but instead serve his sentence at another premises, subject to the relevant procedures.
He also referred to the Pardons Board’s previous decision to reduce Najib’s 12-year prison sentence to six years and his RM210 million fine to RM50 million.

Saifuddin said the ministry had subsequently informed Najib that if he paid the reduced RM50 million fine, his release date would be August 23, 2028, while failure to pay would result in a release date of August 23, 2029.
Saifuddin said Malaysia currently had no specific law governing the mechanism for house arrest.

He said he had previously obtained Cabinet agreement in principle to begin the process of introducing a House Arrest Act, but the proposal was initially intended to address prison overcrowding, particularly involving remand prisoners.
Saifuddin said Malaysia currently had 41 prisons housing about 93,000 inmates, against a total capacity of around 75,000.
Under the proposed mechanism, remand prisoners could potentially be placed under house arrest and monitored through modern electronic devices until their trial dates.
bae37ddfc39b202b: HAVANA: Cuba's electrical grid suffered a total collapse on Friday, plunging the nation into darkness and leaving millions without power amid a US pressure campaign that has largely blocked oil from reaching the Caribbean's largest island.
Friday's collapse was triggered by a failure in high-voltage transmission lines in central Cuba that occurred around 2pm local time, authorities said.
"Protocols are now in place to begin the gradual restoration of the system," said Felix Estrada, an official with Cuba's National Electrical Union (UNE).
Power had returned to a handful of scattered neighbourhoods in Havana by late evening, primarily around hospitals, but much of the city remained completely dark under cloudy skies and rain.
The nationwide blackout, the latest of at least six partial or total grid collapses since January, hardly registered in a country accustomed to long hours, or even days, without power.
Many exhausted residents of the capital Havana were already without power when the blackout hit.

"Yesterday I'd gone without power for 24 hours. They turned the lights on for an hour, and then the grid collapsed," said Frank Lorenzo, a 23-year-old Havana resident looking forward to a long night of sweating and slapping mosquitoes.

Cuba's ageing power generation system has been under severe strain from fuel shortages and decrepit infrastructure for years, but a US-imposed oil blockade that began in January has vastly worsened blackouts and led to more frequent grid collapses.
The grid collapsed three times in July, and rolling blackouts have since spanned 30 hours or more across most of the country.

United Nations human rights experts have condemned the US oil blockade, calling it a violation of international law and warning that Cuba risks becoming a "silent Gaza" as shortages and blackouts grow ever more critical.
7528a6a3adfe6af7: PETALING JAYA: The home ministry has yet to be formally informed by the Federal Territories Pardons Board (FTPB) about allowing Najib Razak to serve his remaining jail term under house arrest if he settles his RM50 million fine.

Home minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the ministry and the prisons department cannot make the necessary preparations until they receive the letter and are informed of the details of the conditional pardon.
"I am still waiting to be informed; usually it comes from the Prime Minister's Department's legal affairs division, which is the FTPB's secretariat.
"Once we've been informed, we'll have clarity on the next steps to execute the decision in line with the legal provisions," he said at a press conference in Kedah today.

He declined to comment if Najib's home at Taman Duta was suitable for him to be placed under house arrest, saying his ministry must first see if the FTPB had already assigned a specific location or left it to the prisons department.
Saifuddin also said Malaysia does not have a specific law concerning house arrest, but pointed out that he was working on a bill to allow house arrests, particularly for remand detainees.
"I had already obtained the Cabinet's agreement in principle to start the process to table a house arrest bill in Parliament.
"If approved, it would allow us to place remand inmates under house arrests, while making them wear devices that allow us to track their movements.
"That was the original intention," he said.
934ff57ef0f52e6f: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 19 — The Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) is stepping up its security readiness and border inspection capabilities ahead of the launch of the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link in January next year.

AKPS director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain said preparations were being intensified through the use of technology, personnel training and operational simulations to ensure effective inspection of documents and goods.
He said that despite the important role of technology in supporting enforcement, it could not be regarded as the sole solution to security threats at the country’s entry points.

“Technology helps, but it is not the solution to these threats. A combination of both is essential, while how we utilise technology for enforcement is equally important, including training,” he told Bernama recently.
Mohd Shuhaily said AKPS would also advise operators on suitable technologies to enhance security and mitigate potential risks.
On the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to help curb the smuggling of illicit goods, he said the technology needs to undergo a learning phase, including machine learning, before reaching maturity.
“Before AI can mature, it needs to learn through what is known as machine learning. So, it is still a work in progress,” he said.
Meanwhile, Mohd Shuhaily said 400 AKPS trainees were currently undergoing a three-month training programme at the Segamat Police Training Centre ahead of their deployment to the RTS Link.
He said the trainees were expected to complete their training by the end of September before being deployed to the RTS Link in October.
“We will conduct dry runs over the remaining two months so that by January, everyone is fully prepared to operate this new facility,” he said.
Mohd Shuhaily said the personnel would initially work alongside senior officers at the Sultan Iskandar Building to gain experience, particularly in inspecting documents and goods. — Bernama
a286725280567bcf: PETALING JAYA: Timbalan Presiden Amanah Mujahid Yusof Rawa mempersoalkan kompas moral Umno dan PAS susulan reaksi kedua-dua parti itu terhadap pengampunan bersyarat bekas perdana menteri Najib Razak.

Bekas menteri agama itu berkata, beliau menghormati keputusan Yang di-Pertuan Agong mengurniakan pengampunan bersyarat itu, namun amat bimbang melihat cara Umno dan PAS meraikan keputusan itu seolah-olah suatu kemenangan.

"Di mana maruah kita apabila sabitan kesalahan seperti ini tidak lagi menjadi perkara yang memalukan, tetapi disambut dengan kemenangan, kemenangan meraikan seorang yang sabit kesalahannya di mahkamah?" soalnya dalam kenyataan.

"Lebih membimbangkan apabila Umno mula mengutip wang ahli untuk membantu pesalah membayar denda RM50 juta. Ini bukan kutipan membantu orang miskin atau orang yang ditimpa musibah. Ini kutipan untuk membantu seorang bekas perdana menteri yang didapati bersalah daripada sabitan mahkamah."
Mujahid berkata, Umno dan PAS mesti membezakan antara menghormati keputusan Agong dengan tindakan meraikan seorang pemimpin yang sabitan kesalahannya masih kekal dalam rekod.
Tambahnya, kehilangan keberanian moral untuk berpendirian tegas menentang rasuah hanya akan menyebabkan Umno dan PAS tidak lagi mampu membela maruah bangsa Melayu dan umat Islam.
"Apa sudah jadi kepada kompas moral politik orang Melayu kita? Tiba masanya orang Melayu membuat keputusan penting perihal maruah mereka," katanya.
"Jangan biarkan maruah Melayu diperwakilkan kepada mereka yang menormalisasikan jenayah, kelak generasi hadapan akan menganggap jenayah rasuah adalah satu keperwiraan bagi orang-orang Melayu."

Umno dan PAS sebelum ini menyambut baik pengampunan bersyarat Najib, dengan Umno melancarkan tabung kutipan kilat bagi membantu bekas presidennya itu melunaskan denda RM50 juta supaya dia boleh menjalani baki hukuman penjara sebagai tahanan di rumah.
Presiden Umno Zahid Hamidi, turut menzahirkan harapan agar perkembangan ini dapat menyuntik momentum kepada Barisan Nasional (BN) menjelang PRN Melaka akan datang.
Sementara itu, PAS menyatakan rasa syukur atas pengampunan Najib kerana percaya bekas perdana menteri itu masih mampu menyumbang kepada negara walaupun berstatus tahanan di rumah.

Wawasan, yang juga komponen Perikatan Nasional (PN), menzahirkan rasa lega kerana keputusan itu berjaya menoktahkan polemik berhubung isu pengampunan Najib, manakala satu lagi parti anggota PN, Pejuang, menggesa penjelasan terperinci mengenai mekanisme serta syarat yang melayakkan banduan menjalani tahanan di rumah.
51fbf6a92631eb75: ANKARA, Sept 19 — Turkiye has revoked the licence of Iran’s Bank Mellat, a semi-private financial entity that has been subject to Western sanctions for years, the official gazette said early on Saturday.

The decision was announced some two weeks after Washington slapped sanctions on a Turkish bank over alleged ties to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), although it was not immediately clear whether the two issues were related.

The move follows a decision by Turkiye’s banking regulator over the Tehran-based bank, which provides financial support to Iran’s government and is subject to US, EU and UK sanctions, according to OpenSanctions, an open-source database of information on sanctions-hit entities.
The Iranian government is also the largest shareholder of the bank, it said.

In revoking Bank Mellat’s licence, the Turkish regulator cited article 71b of the banking law, which says the entity’s “continued operation poses a threat to the rights of depositors and participation fund holders and to the security and stability of the financial system”.
Bank Mellat has been subjected to Western sanctions for years over accusations Tehran was pursuing an atomic weapon under the cover of a civil nuclear programme.
Those sanctions were lifted as part of a landmark 2015 deal between Tehran and world powers to curb its nuclear ambitions.
But the US unilaterally pulled out of the deal in May 2018, reimposing biting economic sanctions on Iran.
Bank Mellat was also hit by US and Gulf sanctions in 2019 after being named as one of 25 entities linked to Iran’s Revolutionary Guards.
On September 4, the US Treasury Department imposed sanctions on Turkiye’s Golden Global Bank over its alleged ties to the Revolutionary Guards as it sought to step up financial pressure on Iran.
The Turkish investment bank denied the accusations.
Iran has been at war since late February, when the United States and Israel launched a surprise bombing campaign that killed the Islamic republic’s supreme leader.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has said Washington was declaring an “economic D-Day” on Iran, warning of harsh consequences for countries that do not join the campaign.

The move by Turkiye’s banking regulator comes just days before President Recep Tayyip Erdogan is reportedly due to hold talks with US President Donald Trump on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly which begins in New York on Tuesday. — AFP
0bf6ecaee74a0adb: PETALING JAYA: Amanah deputy president Mujahid Yusof Rawa has questioned the moral compass of Umno and PAS following their reaction to former prime minister Najib Razak's conditional pardon.

The former religious affairs minister said he respected the king's decision to grant Najib the conditional pardon, but found the way Umno and PAS celebrated the decision as a victory of sorts "very concerning".
"Where is our dignity when being convicted of corruption is no longer an embarrassment but is celebrated ... when we celebrate someone convicted by the courts?

"What's even more concerning is Umno raising funds from the public to help this convict pay his RM50 million fine. This isn't a fundraiser for the poor or those affected by disasters. This is to help a convicted former prime minister," he said in a statement.
Mujahid said Umno and PAS must differentiate between respecting the king's decision and celebrating a leader whose conviction remains on record.
He said losing the moral bravery to take a firm stance against corruption would render Umno and PAS incapable of defending the dignity of the Malays and Muslims.
"What has happened to the moral compass of our Malay people? It's time the Malays make an important decision for the sake of their dignity.
"Don't allow Malay dignity to be represented by those who normalise crime, otherwise our future generations will consider corruption as heroics for the Malay people," he said.

Umno and PAS had welcomed Najib's conditional pardon, with the former launching a fund to help its former president settle his RM50 million fine to allow him to serve his remaining jail term under house arrest.
Umno president Ahmad Zahid Hamidi also expressed hope the development will boost Barisan Nasional's momentum in the upcoming Melaka election.
PAS said it was grateful for Najib's pardon as it believed he could contribute to the country even while he remains under house arrest.

Fellow Perikatan Nasional component Wawasan said it was grateful the decision puts to an end the polemic surrounding Najib's pardon, while another PN member, Pejuang, called for clarity on the mechanism and conditions for inmates to be granted house arrests.
ee300f0a3b4d76f2: SEBERANG PERAI: Fourteen out of the 20 banks in the country have begun offering a reducing balance method for customers with hire purchase loans, in compliance with amendments made to the Hire-Purchase Act.

Domestic trade and cost of living minister Armizan Mohd Ali said the remaining six banks have committed to finalising their transition from the old flat-rate and the Rule of 78 calculation methods to the reducing balance method by Dec 31.

Armizan also said 80% of the 429 hire-purchase providers registered under the Association of Hire Purchase Companies Malaysia are transitioning to both the reducing balance method and the effective interest rate.
"The remaining 20% of providers must complete the transition within the given grace period, which ends on March 31, 2027.

"It is mandatory for all hire-purchase providers to enforce the new laws under the amended Hire-Purchase Act," he said at a press conference at the Consumers Festival 2026 at Stadium Batu Kawan here today.
The amendments abolish the Rule of 78 method to calculate early settlements as well as the flat interest rate structure for hire purchase.

The Rule of 78 is a calculation method to determine the interest rebate for early settlements of hire purchase loans, where a larger portion of the interest is allocated to the earlier instalments of the loan.
This results in borrowers who wish to settle their loans early bearing a high outstanding balance that does not reflect the actual cost of the loan.
Under the reducing balance method mandated by the amended Act, interest charges will be calculated based on the outstanding principal amount.
3bda023367c5b8a4: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 19 — Six foreign men were charged in absentia at the Sessions Court here yesterday with armed gang robbery at a residential unit in Pavilion Embassy here on Sept 7.

Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the charge was framed under Sections 395 and 397 of the Penal Code, which carry a maximum sentence of 20 years’ imprisonment and whipping upon conviction.
“During yesterday’s proceedings, the Deputy Public Prosecutor applied for arrest warrants for all the accused.
“The court subsequently set Oct 16 for mention of the application for the arrest warrants,” he said in a statement today.
Fadil said police would apply for an Interpol Red Notice to track down and arrest all the suspects.
He said police received a report on Sept 7 from a 28-year-old Chinese national who was robbed at his residence at about 5.31pm.
Fadil said the investigation papers were referred to the Kuala Lumpur Federal Territory Prosecution Office on Sept 17.
He urged anyone with information on the suspects’ movements or whereabouts to contact the nearest police station immediately to assist in the investigation. — Bernama
876463c507a4696b: TEHRAN, Sept 19 — Iran’s judiciary announced on Saturday the execution of a man accused of providing information about Iranian missile sites to Israeli intelligence.

“The death penalty was carried out against Hossein Pedaran, who had provided the Mossad with information on missile sites in Isfahan province” in central Iran, judicial authorities said, without saying when he was arrested or put on trial.
Pedaran had faced accusations of “espionage and intelligence collaboration” in favour of Israel.
The judiciary said his sentence had been upheld by the Supreme Court.
The case had not previously been reported by the media.
Iranian authorities have escalated arrests and executions both in connection with the Middle East war that began in February and the nationwide protests that peaked in January.
Throughout the war, numerous missile sites have been bombed. Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was killed at the start of the war.
Isfahan province, which hosts Iranian nuclear sites, has been one of the hardest hit throughout the war.
In August, the judiciary announced the execution of two men accused of having “transmitted the coordinates of sensitive military and security sites” to Israel.
Iran carries out the second highest number of executions in the world after China, according to rights groups. — AFP

54c660d30a10a5c5: NAGOYA: Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) president Sheikh Joaan bin Hamad Al Thani said on Saturday that politicians should not be involved in sports, following a diplomatic incident involving a Taiwan government official at the Asian Games.

Taiwan sport minister Lee Yang, a former Olympic badminton champion, was initially blocked from attending a flag-raising ceremony at the Games on Friday, triggering a standoff as the Taiwan delegation refused to participate in protest.

Lee was eventually permitted entry, with the ceremony taking place more than an hour after scheduled. Taiwan's cabinet complained Lee had been subject to "unreasonable obstruction" in a statement and that he had obtained the required access credentials.
Sheikh Joaan said at a press conference he was unaware of the incident but that politicians needed to stay out of sports at the quadrennial Games.

"I think that our focus here is on the athletes and on making sure that everyone, all the athletes, has the equal rights in competing and in having their freedom," the Qatari told reporters in Nagoya.
"So I don't think the politicians or politics should be involved in sports. That's my opinion."
OCA director general Husain Al-Musallam added that the flag-raising ceremony was meant for the participants in the Games.
"(It's) not for the delegation from the ministry or from the government," he said.
Lee claimed back-to-back badminton gold medals in the men's doubles at the Tokyo and Paris Olympics.
The buildup to the Aichi-Nagoya Games has been overshadowed by complaints from national team delegations over organisational issues, including transport and the accommodations provided for athletes.
Sheikh Joaan defended the local organisers saying they had been solving accommodation issues as they arise.
"I think everything is hopefully being back on track," he said.
The organisational problems have underscored the massive size of the Games, which include a record 43 sports and 469 medal events, dwarfing the summer Olympics' 32 sports and 329 events.
The OCA defended the size of the programme at Nagoya, which will see the debut of "virtual" taekwondo while retaining breaking (breakdancing) and esports.
"We are very proud that the Asian Games are bigger than any other games with low cost," said Al-Musallam.
bfaf8008ecfc2254: Mozilla and MZLA have delivered the latest releases in their new fortnightly cycle, but users who dislike the faster pace have alternatives. Firefox 156 is trickling out to users. The release notes only mention two new features: for Mac users, there's now an option in Settings to automatically launch the app at login. This vulture has received criticism for saying this in some of the product's forums before, but since pretty much every OS has a built-in facility for this, we don't really see the point – though it's harmless and could be handy. Users who have chosen French, German or Italian will now find suggestions from Wikipedia in their own languages – along with potentially less welcome ads from Mozilla partners. If you don't want such suggestions, you can turn them off in Firefox Suggest settings. As with the previous release of both apps, the changes in Thunderbird sound slightly more useful – but again, they are small. Thunderbird 156 offers more troubleshooting info in the event of problems with OpenPGP, and more options for OAuth authorization for POP3 and IMAP accounts. There are also additional enterprise policies for controlling filters and user customizations. As we said last time, though, users who want to get off the rapid-upgrade train have several options. The most obvious comes directly from Mozilla: the Firefox ESR and Thunderbird ESR versions only get security fixes, with full new versions only coming annually. Currently, both are on version 153, which appeared in late July. A fistful of forks There aren't many Thunderbird-based messaging clients, possibly because so many people now use webmail. The main Thunderbird fork is Betterbird. Its current version is based on the current Thunderbird ESR, version 153. There are Windows, Linux, and Mac versions, including a portable edition for Windows. Portable Betterbird runs directly from a USB drive without installation or administrator rights, allowing users to carry their message database between computers. There are quite a few alternative browsers based on Firefox, though. The Reg FOSS desk has been using Waterfox on our Linux machines ever since Firefox Quantum appeared back in 2017. That release, Firefox 57, broke 90 percent of our meticulously assembled collection of more than 30 extensions. Waterfox Classic preserved support for the legacy extensions that Firefox Quantum abandoned and continued receiving maintenance for several years. It remained compatible with those older XUL-based extensions for years after Firefox abandoned them, giving the extension builders time to catch up. Waterfox Classic has been unmaintained since 2022 and is no longer recommended. The current Waterfox release, version 6.7, is based on Firefox 153 ESR. If you want a Firefox-like browser with no AI, a built-in ad-blocker and tree-style tabs, and a slower-moving, more stable release schedule, then Waterfox is worth a look. A detail that we like about Waterfox is that it still works fine with a global menu bar, whether that's in Ubuntu Unity or in a customized Xfce profile. LibreWolf is a customized privacy-centric build of Firefox with less telemetry. It remains close to the parent project, and new versions are keeping pace with Mozilla's faster release cadence. So if you don't mind the faster releases, but do want even more privacy, LibreWolf could be a good option. If you want a fancier, more customizable UI, then the Japanese Floorp browser is another option. It has its own release cycle and, at the time of writing, is up to version 12.17.2, which incorporates the changes in Firefox 155. Floorp features multiple sidebars and other UI customizations over and above what's possible with Firefox or any of the other forks. If you want a less-cluttered UI rather than more toolbars and more gadgets, then the Zen Browser may be more your thing. It is more minimal than Floorp, but in some ways more radical. Its main selling point is the ability to tile multiple web pages, so you can see them all on screen at the same time. Otherwise, it exposes less interface clutter than other Firefox variants. We looked at it in 2024 and it's only got better since then. If you use an OS with tiling window management, or an optional extra such as Rectangle for macOS or Mosaic for GNOME, you may not need Zen, but it has its own advantages. You do not need to be a Mullvad VPN customer to use the Mullvad browser. However, prospective users may object to the politics of one of its co-founders. As we reported recently, Daniel Berntsson recently made a large and controversial donation to a Swedish anti-immigration party. Of course, you may also be indifferent to the political views of the company's owners. The Mullvad browser was co-developed with the Tor Project, and for the ultimate in online anonymity and invisibility, that project also offers the Tor Browser. It's probably overkill for daily use, though. And there's more… There is also an assortment of more specialized forks drawing on Mozilla's code and that of some of the projects above. A decade-long trademark dispute between Mozilla and Debian led to Debian maintaining its own version of Firefox with all Mozilla branding removed. This was settled in 2016, but variants of the project are still in development. IceWeasel is a debranded Firefox with some tweaks and optimizations, available for x86-64 Windows and Linux. The GNU Project also maintains a debranded fork, called GNU IceCat, as well as a version of the old Mozilla Internet Suite. They are only packaged for the GNU Guix distribution, which we looked at along with its init system in 2024. There is also a separately maintained Debian package. The FireDragon browser incorporates LibreWolf's privacy adjustments and modifies the UI to better suit the Garuda Linux distribution – an Arch variant that rather impressed us back in 2022. Despite its Garuda origins, FireDragon is available for all major operating systems. It follows its own versioning system, under which it's currently at version 13.5.1, but it's up to date with the parent project. Betterfox isn't a fork, but a set of configuration files that you can download and apply to an existing Firefox installation. Older versions, older OSes, and older processors Not all of the changes in Mozilla's products over the years have won over all their users – such as the "Australis" theme that The Register mentioned back in 2012. The Pale Moon browser forked from Firefox long before even Firefox Quantum; it retains the look and feel of Firefox from version 4 to version 28, which is no longer available in Firefox itself. We first mentioned Pale Moon back in 2021 and again in connection with Cloudflare issues last year. It's actively maintained and current. There's also the Basilisk Browser, forked from a newer version of Firefox than Pale Moon and now maintained independently. Both of these support some older versions of Windows and macOS than modern Firefox. When we wrote about running Windows XP in 2023, we mentioned the MyPal68 browser, a fork of relatively recent Firefox that still works on 32-bit Windows all the way back to Windows XP – as well as on 64-bit versions, naturally. MyPal68 is still in active maintenance and it's now up to version 78.1.0. There's R3dfox too, a custom fork of Firefox for those who prefer Windows Vista and Windows 7. The latest release is based on Firefox 153, the current ESR version. For users of old versions of Mac OS X, there are multiple options. Momiji is an actively maintained version of Firefox 140 ESR that runs on OS X 10.7 "Lion" and later. It continues the work of the Firefox Dynasty project, which we mentioned a year ago as an option for older Macs. Powerfox is similar: it targets Intel-based Macs and is based on the newer Firefox 153 ESR. The project also offers Powerfox Classic, which supports PowerMacs running all the way back to Mac OS X 10.3 "Panther." Aquafox is a modernized version of TenFourFox, for PowerMacs with Mac OS X 10.4. The SeaMonkey Project is a fork that continues development of the original pre-Firefox Mozilla Internet Suite: it's not just a web browser, but also contains an email/USENET client, an IRC client, an RSS reader, and a WYSIWYG HTML editor. It's still maintained, it's now 64-bit only, and it supports all major OSes – but compatibility may be an issue, as it uses a very old version of the Gecko rendering engine. We also found several Firefox forks that appear to be unmaintained and are probably best avoided. In addition to its ad blocker, Ghostery once offered a separate Ghostery Private Browser, but discontinued development in 2024. Similarly, the Mercury Browser for Windows and Linux was a more private Firefox with compiler optimizations so it ran faster. It never progressed beyond version 129, released a couple of years ago. The Cyberfox Browser was a 64-bit Windows version back when Mozilla didn't offer such things, although the project also offered a 32-bit version. It hasn't had a new release in eight years. Plasmafox was Firefox tweaked to better integrate with the KDE Plasma desktop on Arch Linux, but it fell off its perch after version 88.0.1, five years ago. These are the only ones of which the news has come to The Reg FOSS desk– although there may be many others. If we've missed any, do please let us know. ®
02da881469998919: MIRI, Sept 19 — The Air Accident Investigation Bureau (BSKU) will issue a preliminary report on the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash on September 8 within 30 days of the accident, in accordance with Annex 13 of the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) on Aircraft Accident and Incident Investigation.
Deputy Minister for Transport Datuk Hasbi Habibollah said the preliminary report would subsequently be presented to the Cabinet, in line with the Cabinet’s decision on September 9.

“BSKU will issue a preliminary report within 30 days from the date of the accident, in accordance with ICAO Annex 13,” he told reporters when met at a function in Long Lama on Saturday (September 19).
Hasbi added that the BSKU was currently conducting a technical investigation in accordance with ICAO Annex 13 and Part XXVI of the Civil Aviation Regulations 2016.
He said BSKU investigators had gone to the crash site to examine the site and aircraft wreckage, as well as collect and preserve evidence.

“The investigation covers examination of the crash site and aircraft wreckage, the collection and preservation of evidence, a review of operational and maintenance records, crew information, weather conditions and other relevant evidence,” he said.

He said the investigation was also receiving technical cooperation and support from the aircraft manufacturer in Germany and the engine manufacturer in the United States, in accordance with ICAO Annex 13.
He stressed that the cause of the accident and any contributing factors had yet to be determined.
“At this stage, the cause and contributing factors of the accident have yet to be determined.
“The investigation is ongoing and BSKU will not draw any conclusions until all the evidence has been examined,” he said.
On September 8, a Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crashed at the Long Lellang STOLport at around 3.40pm, killing all five crew members on board.

The victims were identified as pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30; medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33; assistant medical officer Alexson Adit Henry, 31; as well as staff nurses Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44. — The Borneo Post
8ebeb2fe36eb6d25: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 19 — The ringgit is likely to remain range-bound against the US dollar next week, with market attention drawn to speeches by several US Federal Reserve (Fed) officials, an analyst said.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid noted that a series of Fed officials are expected to share their thoughts with the public.
More insights can perhaps be gleaned on their thought process when the risk of higher fuel prices is likely to stay, he told Bernama.
According to the latest US Fed forecast, there would be another 25-basis point hike this year, said Mohd Afzanizam.
“Hence, we will see the degree of conviction for rate hike in the months to come.
“On that note, (trading in) the ringgit is expected to stay cautious next week. We foresee the ringgit-dollar (rate) to range between RM4.06 and RM4.09 next week,” he said.
Meanwhile, on a Friday-to-Friday basis, the ringgit weakened against the greenback to 4.0795/0840 from 4.0685/0725 a week earlier.
However, the local currency traded higher against a basket of major currencies during the week.

The ringgit appreciated versus the British pound to 5.4543/4603 from 5.4961/5015 on the previous Friday, gained against the Japanese yen to 2.5829/5860 from 2.6400/6428, and rose vis-a-vis the euro to 4.6849/6901 from 4.7178/7225.
It also traded mostly higher against Asean currencies.

1a394196cd19bf5d: NAGOYA, Sept 19 — The 20th Asian Games will open in Japan later Saturday with a glittering ceremony following a stuttering build-up to a multi-sport spectacular that has more participants than the Olympics.
The first gold medal will be won on Sunday morning, likely in the men’s individual triathlon, and will be followed by 468 more in more than 40 sports before the curtain comes down on October 4.
The event in Nagoya and Aichi prefecture has 2028 Olympics places up for grabs in seven sports and will be graced by global stars.
But it has been dogged by a series of problems in the lead-up.
The 17,000 participants – more than the Olympics – stretched organisers to the limit as they scrambled to find accommodation for everyone.
To save money, there is no traditional athletes’ village, with competitors instead staying in a combination of temporary container-style huts, hotels and the cruise ship Costa Serena.

To add to the issues, there was a record deluge last week which flooded parts of Nagoya city, while a tropical storm is approaching eastern Japan and could cause further disruption on Sunday and Monday.
Some athletes were left stranded at the airport when transport failed to turn up, while several teams have complained about the quality of the huts, including beds being too short.
In the latest mishap, North Korea’s national anthem was played on Friday for South Korea’s men’s hockey team.
“This is a really serious problem,” said South Korea coach Min Tae-seok.
On Saturday, with the opening ceremony hours away, India drafted in a new flag-bearer after shot-putter Tajinderpal Singh Toor’s luggage did not have his ceremonial kit.
Kabaddi player Pawan Sehrawat will replace him, Indian media said.
‘Most spectacular’

Former ‘yokozuna’ Hakuho carries the flame during the torch relay ahead of the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya on September 18, 2026. — Jiji Press pic via AFP
Organisers are insisting that the latest edition of the Games, which were first held in 1951, will be “the most spectacular for generations”.
Basketball, football and cricket are among the sports already under way.
As always at the Asian Games, Olympic staples such as athletics and swimming will sit side-by-side with regional favourites like sepak takraw and kabaddi.
In a bid to attract younger viewers, there will be eSports, breakdancing and BMX cycling.
Padel, the fast-growing racquet sport, and MMA will make their Asian Games debuts.
Among those competing will be Philippine tennis sensation Alexandra Eala and a pair of prodigies in 15-year-old Indian cricketer Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and 13-year-old Chinese swimmer Yu Zidi.
Yu will be in action in the pool straightaway on Sunday in the heats of the women’s 200m butterfly.
Taiwan boxer Lin Yu-ting will also be competing, two years after she won Paris Olympics gold in the middle of a major gender row that saw her eligibility questioned.
Hosts Japan will look to their Olympic champions for success, with gymnast Shinnosuke Oka and javelin thrower Haruka Kitaguchi named in their team.
North Korea will have more than 100 athletes competing across 14 sports, aiming to “bring joy to Marshal Kim Jong Un”.
China will again expect to top the medals table after winning a whopping 201 golds and 383 medals on home soil in Hangzhou at the Covid-delayed Games in 2023.
They are sending more than 800 athletes, including 36 Olympic champions.
Sooryavanshi will be part of an India cricket team looking to make a statement before the sport returns to the Olympics in Los Angeles after an absence of 128 years.
India could face bitter rivals Pakistan in the final at Nagoya’s new purpose-built cricket ground — if forecast rain does not intervene. — AFP
